title: World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp 2026: Fully Funded Seoul Programme for Government Institutions in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
summary: The World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp for Governance and Public Administration 2026 is inviting government institutions from low- and middle-income countries to submit proposals for an intensive, fully funded technical bootcamp focused on the practical use of artificial intelligence in government and public administration. The initiative is being organized by the World Bank , the Republic of Korea’s Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS) , and the National Information Society Agency (NIA) . It is designed for government institutions that are already developing, piloting, or deploying AI-enabled solutions aimed at improving public-sector performance, service delivery, transparency, efficiency, citizen engagement, and other areas of governance. Up to five government teams will be selected to participate in a five-day technical bootcamp in Seoul, South Korea, from December 7 to 11, 2026 . The programme provides participants with an opportunity to learn directly from Korean public-sector practitioners and technology experts who have experience designing, implementing, and scaling digital and AI systems across government. Participants will also engage with World Bank experts and other relevant stakeholders to strengthen their own AI initiatives and develop practical implementation roadmaps. The application deadline is October 2, 2026 . Overview of the World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp Artificial intelligence is increasingly becoming an important tool for transforming public administration. Governments around the world are exploring how AI can improve the way public institutions deliver services, manage resources, interact with citizens, combat corruption, process information, and make evidence-based decisions. However, having an AI strategy is only one part of the process. Governments also need the technical capacity, institutional arrangements, data infrastructure, governance mechanisms, procurement systems, human resources, and implementation plans required to translate AI strategies into functioning public-sector solutions. The World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp has been designed to address this implementation gap. Rather than focusing solely on theoretical discussions about artificial intelligence, the programme emphasizes practical implementation, technical problem-solving, peer learning, institutional coordination, and knowledge exchange . Selected government teams will have the opportunity to examine Korea’s experience in deploying AI and digital government systems and apply relevant lessons to their own public-sector initiatives. What Is the GovTech AI Bootcamp? The GovTech AI Bootcamp is an international technical learning and implementation programme focused on helping governments strengthen AI-enabled solutions in governance and public administration. The programme brings together selected government teams with: World Bank governance and GovTech experts; Korean government practitioners; Korean public-sector institutions; Technology and AI practitioners; Relevant private-sector technology providers where appropriate; and Other experts involved in the design, deployment, governance, and scaling of public-sector AI systems. The programme combines exposure to Korea’s AI ecosystem with hands-on technical workshops. Participants will not simply attend presentations. They will be expected to examine their own government initiative, identify implementation challenges, explore potential solutions, and develop a technically grounded roadmap for moving their initiative forward. Who Should Apply? The call is specifically aimed at government institutions in low- and middle-income countries that are pursuing AI initiatives in public administration. Eligible initiatives may cover a wide range of government functions, including: Public Financial Management Government institutions working on AI applications related to budgeting, financial management, expenditure management, revenue administration, auditing, financial forecasting, or other public financial management functions may be eligible. Civil Service and Human Resource Management Applications may focus on AI-enabled systems for government human-resource management, workforce planning, recruitment, personnel administration, skills management, or related civil-service functions. Citizen Services Government institutions developing AI solutions to improve public services and make interactions between citizens and government institutions more efficient may apply. Civic Technology and Citizen Engagement AI initiatives aimed at improving citizen participation, government responsiveness, public communication, feedback mechanisms, or engagement with communities may also be considered. Public Procurement Government institutions exploring AI for procurement processes, supplier management, fraud detection, procurement efficiency, or related public-sector functions may be eligible. Anti-Corruption AI initiatives designed to identify risks, detect irregularities, improve oversight, strengthen accountability, or support anti-corruption efforts can fall within the scope of the programme. Transparency and Accountability Government projects using AI to improve transparency, access to information, monitoring, accountability, or public-sector oversight may also qualify. Other Public-Sector Applications The opportunity is not limited to the examples above. Other AI-enabled public-sector applications may be considered where they demonstrate a clear governance or public-administration challenge and a credible pathway toward implementation. Team Composition Requirements Each application must nominate a two-person government team . The team should consist of: 1. A Policy Leader The policy leader should have sufficient institutional authority and decision-making responsibility to influence or support the implementation of the proposed AI initiative. This individual should be able to understand the policy and institutional dimensions of the project and help ensure that lessons from the bootcamp can be translated into organizational action. 2. A Technical Practitioner The second team member should be a technical practitioner who is directly involved in implementing the proposed AI initiative. This could be someone working on areas such as the following: Artificial intelligence; Data systems; Digital government; Information technology; Software development; Data management; Digital transformation; Public-sector technology implementation; or Related technical functions. The combination of a policy leader and technical practitioner is important because successful government AI implementation requires both institutional decision-making and technical expertise . What Makes a Strong Application? The selection process will place considerable emphasis on the quality and feasibility of the proposed AI initiative. A strong proposal should demonstrate a clearly defined public-sector implementation challenge rather than simply expressing a general interest in artificial intelligence. The proposed initiative should also have progressed beyond an entirely conceptual stage. In particular, strong applications are expected to demonstrate that the proposed AI solution is: Already being developed; Being piloted; or Already being deployed. Applicants should clearly explain the problem they are trying to solve, why AI is relevant to addressing the problem, what has already been achieved, and what barriers remain. Institutional Commitment Applicants should demonstrate that their institution is genuinely committed to the proposed initiative. Institutional commitment can be particularly important when implementing AI within government because successful deployment often requires cooperation across departments, leadership support, budgetary resources, policy adjustments, technical capacity, data access, procurement arrangements, and long-term institutional ownership. Technical Feasibility Applications should demonstrate that the proposed solution is technically realistic. Applicants should consider issues such as the following: Data availability and quality; Digital infrastructure; System architecture; Technical capacity; Algorithms and models; Cybersecurity and data governance; Integration with existing government systems; Human-resource requirements; and Potential implementation constraints. Clear Implementation Pathway The proposal should demonstrate how the initiative can move from its current stage toward practical implementation or scale. Applicants should identify the most important barriers and explain how participation in the bootcamp could help address those barriers. Why Participate in the GovTech AI Bootcamp? The programme offers selected government institutions an opportunity to combine international knowledge with practical technical support. Learn From Korea’s Public-Sector AI Experience South Korea has developed extensive digital government capabilities and has deployed technology across numerous public-sector functions. Participants will have the opportunity to learn from Korean institutions involved in designing and operating public-sector digital and AI systems. This provides participants with an opportunity to understand not only the technology itself, but also the institutional and operational processes required to make AI work within government. Develop a Practical AI Implementation Roadmap One of the central objectives of the bootcamp is to help participating teams develop a practical roadmap for their own AI initiative. The roadmap will address technical and implementation considerations and help teams identify the steps required to move their projects forward. Identify Technical and Data Challenges AI implementation can be constrained by problems involving data, algorithms, infrastructure, systems integration, technical expertise, and institutional dependencies. During the bootcamp, participants will work with experts to examine these challenges and develop approaches for addressing them. Engage With World Bank Experts Selected participants will interact with World Bank experts working in governance, GovTech, public-sector innovation, and related areas. This provides an opportunity to receive perspectives from an international development institution with extensive experience supporting digital transformation and institutional reform. Build International Peer Connections The programme also creates opportunities for participating government teams to exchange experiences and lessons with other institutions working on AI-enabled public-sector transformation. This type of peer learning can help governments identify common implementation challenges and discover approaches that may be adapted to their own contexts. Potential Follow-Up Technical Support Following the Seoul bootcamp, participating teams may receive follow-up support and technical feedback. This support will depend on the strength and viability of proposals and the recommendations and expert advice developed during the programme. Why Is Korea the Host Country? Korea has become internationally recognized for its advanced digital government ecosystem and the large-scale deployment of technology across public administration. Its experience includes the use of digital systems and emerging technologies in areas such as: Public financial management; Tax administration; Citizen services; Social welfare; Government administration; Digital public services; and Other core government functions. The bootcamp therefore provides participants with the opportunity to move beyond theoretical learning and observe how digital and AI systems operate within real public-sector environments. Participants will engage with Korean public and private institutions involved in the design, operation, and scaling of these systems. Where relevant, participants may also engage with technology providers to gain insight into the practical requirements associated with system deployment. GovTech AI Bootcamp Programme Structure The programme is divided into three major phases. Phase One: Call for Proposals The first phase involves the submission and evaluation of applications. Government institutions are required to explain their AI initiatives and the public-sector implementation challenges they are currently facing. Applicants should provide sufficient information to allow the selection committee to assess: The public-sector problem; The proposed AI solution; Current stage of development; Technical readiness; Data readiness; Institutional support; Implementation risks; Expected benefits; Learning objectives; and Planned activities after the bootcamp. The application deadline for this phase is October 2, 2026 . Following the evaluation process, selected teams will be notified of the outcome. Phase Two: Seoul Bootcamp The second phase is the five-day programme in Seoul scheduled for December 7–11, 2026 The Seoul programme will combine exposure to Korea s public and private AI ecosystem with practical technical learning. Participants will take part in site visits and exchanges with practitioners who are responsible for implementing AI and digital government solutions. The programme will then move into a hands-on workshop environment. During the workshop, participating teams will work with Korean AI practitioners and World Bank experts to refine their approaches and address practical implementation issues. The technical work may include practical coding exercises and examination of: Algorithmic bottlenecks; Data challenges; Infrastructure requirements; Technical dependencies; Implementation risks; Institutional dependencies; Contingency planning; and Strategies for successful deployment. The objective is to ensure that participating teams leave the bootcamp with a roadmap grounded in practical implementation considerations. Phase Three: Follow-Up Support The third phase takes place after the Seoul bootcamp. Selected teams may receive follow-up technical support and feedback to help them advance their AI initiatives. The availability and nature of this support will depend on factors including the strength and viability of the proposals and the expert recommendations developed during the bootcamp. This means the opportunity can potentially extend beyond the five-day programme itself, providing selected teams with additional assistance as they work toward implementation. Key Dates for the World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp 2026 Applicants should carefully note the important dates associated with the programme. Activity Date Launch of Call for Proposals August 12, 2026 Application Deadline October 2, 2026 Notification of Results October 16, 2026 Seoul Bootcamp December 7–11, 2026 Final Roadmap Submission January 23, 2027 Selection of Follow-Up Support Teams February 13, 2027 The most important date for prospective applicants is October 2, 2026 , which is the deadline for submitting proposals. What Information Will Applicants Need to Provide? Applicants will be expected to provide information that allows the organizers to understand both the proposed AI initiative and the institution s ability to implement it. The application is expected to address areas such as the following: Public-Sector Challenge Applicants should clearly explain the government problem or implementation challenge they are trying to address. The challenge should be specific and demonstrate why intervention is necessary. Proposed AI Solution The application should explain the proposed AI-enabled solution and how it is expected to address the identified challenge. Applicants should avoid presenting AI simply as a technological trend. Instead, they should demonstrate a clear connection between the technology and the public-sector outcome they want to achieve. Technical and Data Readiness Applicants should describe the current state of their technology, data, systems, infrastructure, and technical capacity. This is particularly important because AI solutions depend heavily on reliable and accessible data and suitable technical infrastructure. Institutional Support Applicants should explain the level of institutional commitment behind the initiative. This could include leadership support, organizational ownership, existing implementation structures, technical teams, funding arrangements, or other relevant commitments. Implementation Risks Applicants should identify potential risks that could prevent the successful development, deployment, or scaling of the AI initiative. These could include: Data limitations; Technical constraints; Institutional resistance; Skills shortages; Budget limitations; Procurement challenges; Regulatory barriers; Infrastructure limitations; or Coordination challenges. Learning Objectives Applicants should explain what they hope to learn from the bootcamp and how that learning will contribute to their initiative. The strongest applications are likely to connect their learning objectives directly to their existing implementation challenges. Post-Bootcamp Plans Applicants should explain what they intend to do after returning from the Seoul programme. A clear post-bootcamp plan can demonstrate that participation will contribute to actual implementation rather than being treated solely as a learning opportunity. Supporting Documents Applicants may also provide supporting materials that strengthen their proposal. These may include: Institutional endorsement letters; Technical diagrams; Policy documents; Budget commitments; Project documentation; Implementation plans; Relevant research; Technical assessments; or Other documents supporting the proposed initiative. Supporting materials should help demonstrate the credibility, feasibility, and institutional commitment behind the application. Selection Process Applications will be reviewed by representatives from the World Bank, MOIS, and NIA . The selection process will focus on the quality and practical potential of the proposed initiatives. Strong proposals are expected to demonstrate several important characteristics. A Clearly Defined Challenge The proposal should address a genuine and clearly articulated public-sector problem. A Realistic AI Solution The proposed AI solution should be technically and institutionally realistic. Evidence of Existing Development The initiative should already be under development, in a pilot phase, or deployed. Institutional Commitment The government institution should demonstrate meaningful commitment to implementing the initiative. Technical Feasibility The project should have a credible technical foundation and a reasonable pathway toward implementation. Potential for Impact The proposed solution should have the potential to generate meaningful improvements in government operations, public services, transparency, efficiency, citizen engagement, or another relevant public-sector outcome. Clear Benefit From Korean Experience Applicants should explain why exposure to Korea s AI and GovTech experience would be particularly valuable for their initiative. English-Language Participation The bootcamp will be conducted in English , with simultaneous Korean-English interpretation . Participants should therefore be comfortable participating in English-language discussions, workshops, technical sessions, and exchanges. Government institutions should take this into consideration when selecting their two-person team. Who Is Eligible to Apply? This opportunity is intended for government institutions in low- and middle-income countries . It is important to understand that this is not primarily an individual scholarship or fellowship opportunity. The application is made on behalf of a government institution , and the institution must nominate the required two-person team. Eligible applicants should therefore be government institutions with an existing or emerging AI initiative relevant to public administration or governance. Which Countries Can Apply? The call is designed for government institutions from low- and middle-income countries worldwide . The eligibility criterion is therefore based on the country s income classification rather than a specific continent, nationality group, race, or ethnicity. The opportunity is not presented as being restricted to Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East, or any other single geographical region. Government institutions from eligible low- and middle-income countries around the world may therefore consider applying if they meet the substantive requirements of the call. Is There a Race or Ethnicity Requirement? No specific race or ethnicity requirement is stated in the call. The principal eligibility considerations concern: The applicant being a government institution; The institution being located in a low- or middle-income country; The existence of a relevant AI initiative; The initiative being developed, piloted, or deployed; Institutional commitment; Technical feasibility; and The suitability of the nominated two-person team. Is This Opportunity Fully Funded? Yes. The source describes the Seoul bootcamp as a fully funded, five-day technical bootcamp for the selected government teams. Up to five government teams will be selected. Prospective applicants should nevertheless carefully review the official application materials and programme information for the precise arrangements and covered expenses applicable to participating teams. How to Apply for the GovTech AI Bootcamp 2026 Eligible government institutions should submit their applications through the official submission form before the deadline. The application should provide a clear and convincing explanation of the institution s AI initiative and the implementation challenge it is trying to overcome. Applicants should particularly focus on demonstrating: The public-sector problem they are addressing. Why an AI-enabled solution is appropriate. The current stage of development or deployment. The availability and readiness of relevant data. The technical capacity supporting the initiative. Institutional leadership and commitment. Key implementation challenges and risks. What they want to learn from the bootcamp. How Korean experience could help address their challenges. What they plan to do after the programme. The official submission form should be completed by October 2, 2026 . APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp for Governance and Public Administration 2026 is October 2, 2026 . Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their proposals well before the deadline, particularly because government applications may require internal consultations, leadership approval, technical documentation, endorsement letters, and supporting materials. How to Strengthen Your Application Government institutions considering this opportunity should avoid submitting a proposal that simply describes a broad interest in AI. A more competitive application should demonstrate a specific implementation challenge and a concrete solution . For example, applicants should be able to explain: What problem currently exists? Who is affected by the problem? How is the government currently addressing it? What AI-enabled solution is being developed? What stage is the project currently at? What data does the system require? What technical infrastructure is available? What barriers are preventing implementation or scaling? What support is needed? What lessons from Korea could help? What will the institution do after the bootcamp? The clearer these elements are, the easier it becomes for reviewers to understand the practical value and potential impact of the proposed initiative. Important Considerations Before Applying Before submitting a proposal, institutions should confirm that they meet the fundamental requirements. In particular, applicants should consider whether: The applicant is an eligible government institution. The institution is located in a low- or middle-income country. There is an existing AI initiative rather than only a general interest in AI. The initiative is being developed, piloted, or deployed. The proposed initiative addresses a meaningful public-sector challenge. A policy leader with decision-making authority can participate. A technical practitioner directly involved in implementation can participate. The nominated team can participate in English-language activities. The institution has sufficient commitment to advance the initiative after the programme. The team can participate in the Seoul bootcamp from December 7–11, 2026. The application can be completed before October 2, 2026. Frequently Asked Questions Is the GovTech AI Bootcamp open to individuals? The opportunity is primarily intended for government institutions , rather than individuals applying independently. Each institution must nominate a two-person team consisting of a policy leader and a technical practitioner. How many government teams will be selected? Up to five government teams will be selected for the Seoul bootcamp. Where will the bootcamp take place? The five-day bootcamp will take place in Seoul, South Korea . When will the Seoul bootcamp take place? The bootcamp is scheduled for December 7–11, 2026 . What is the application deadline? The application deadline is October 2, 2026 . When will applicants be notified of the results? The notification of results is scheduled for October 16, 2026 . What areas of government can be covered? The call specifically identifies areas such as public financial management, civil service and human resource management, citizen services, civic technology and citizen engagement, procurement, anti-corruption, transparency, and other public-sector applications. Does the AI project have to be fully operational? No. The strongest proposals are expected to involve AI solutions that are already being developed, piloted, or deployed . A project does not necessarily have to be fully operational. Will participants develop an implementation roadmap? Yes. A central component of the hands-on workshop is developing practical and technically grounded implementation roadmaps for the participating initiatives. Can participating teams receive support after the bootcamp? Participating teams may receive follow-up support and technical feedback , depending on the strength and viability of their proposals and the expert advice provided during the programme. Will interpretation be available? Yes. The bootcamp will be conducted in English, with simultaneous Korean-English interpretation . Can applicants provide supporting documents? Yes. Applicants may submit materials such as endorsement letters, technical diagrams, policy documents, budget commitments, and other relevant documentation. Who can applicants contact with questions? Questions not addressed in the official FAQ can be directed to the GovTech team at govtechbootcamp@worldbank.org . Visit HERE for more information about the World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp 2026. Important Official Resources Prospective applicants should consult the official programme information and submission materials before applying. The opportunity is presented through the World Bank s Global Program on GovTech and Public Sector Innovation. The official submission form is the appropriate channel for submitting an application. Conclusion The World Bank GovTech AI Bootcamp for Governance and Public Administration 2026 represents a significant opportunity for eligible government institutions in low- and middle-income countries that are seeking to move AI initiatives from development and pilot stages toward practical implementation and scale. The programme is particularly relevant to institutions that already have a clearly defined public-sector challenge and are developing, piloting, or deploying an AI-enabled solution but require additional technical knowledge, implementation strategies, institutional insights, or exposure to international best practices. By bringing together the World Bank, Korean government institutions, AI practitioners, and selected government teams from eligible countries, the bootcamp provides a platform for practical learning and peer exchange. Participants will gain exposure to Korea s experience in public-sector AI while working directly on the technical and institutional challenges affecting their own initiatives. The opportunity is especially valuable because it goes beyond classroom learning. Participants will have opportunities to engage with practitioners, undertake hands-on technical work, examine data and infrastructure challenges, identify dependencies and risks, and develop implementation roadmaps that can guide their initiatives after the programme. Eligible government institutions should therefore begin preparing their proposals early and ensure that their applications clearly demonstrate the public-sector challenge, AI solution, technical readiness, institutional commitment, implementation pathway, and expected impact . The application deadline is October 2, 2026 , while the selected teams will participate in the Seoul bootcamp from December 7–11, 2026 . For government institutions in eligible low- and middle-income countries already working on practical AI solutions for governance and public administration, this programme offers an opportunity to learn from one of the world s leading digital-government ecosystems and potentially accelerate the implementation of transformative public-sector AI initiatives. title: Shine 2027: Swiss Re Foundation Grant and Accelerator for Early-Stage Urban Climate Innovation
summary: The Swiss Re Foundation Shine 2027 programme is inviting applications from early-stage climate ventures developing innovative solutions to help cities reduce greenhouse gas emissions, adapt to climate change, and create more inclusive, resilient urban communities. Under the 2027 edition, Shine for Cities will support entrepreneurs whose products or services can help address pressing urban climate challenges, including energy transition, sustainable transport, building efficiency, waste and circular economy, urban nature, and climate data and governance. The programme combines grant funding, Swiss Re expertise, business and leadership coaching, climate innovation networks, and support for developing scalable business models . It is designed particularly for ventures that have moved beyond the idea stage and already have a minimum viable product, pilot, or commercial launch underway. Applications for Shine 2027 are open for entrepreneurs operating in or serving one of eight participating cities across Asia, Africa, Europe, North America, and Switzerland. The official programme brochure states that applications should be submitted by 15 September 2026 . What Is Shine 2027? Shine 2027 is the latest edition of the Swiss Re Foundation s flagship Shine initiative, with a specific focus on early-stage innovation for urban climate action . The programme responds to a major challenge facing cities around the world. Urban areas are at the centre of both the climate crisis and the transition towards a more sustainable future. According to the Swiss Re Foundation, cities account for approximately 75% of global greenhouse gas emissions and are home to more than half of the world s population. The urban population is projected to approach 70% of the global population by 2050. At the same time, urban communities are increasingly exposed to climate-related risks such as the following: Extreme heat and heat stress Flooding Resource scarcity Infrastructure disruption Environmental degradation Increasing pressure on urban services Inequality in access to climate-resilient solutions Many cities have already developed climate action plans and established governance systems to respond to these challenges. However, having a plan does not necessarily guarantee implementation. The Swiss Re Foundation identifies this implementation gap as an important opportunity for entrepreneurial innovation. Shine for Cities therefore seeks ventures that can help transform climate ambitions into practical, scalable solutions. Who Is Behind Shine 2027? Shine 2027 is an initiative of the Swiss Re Foundation , which works to strengthen resilience in vulnerable communities and supports entrepreneurial solutions addressing climate and health challenges. The Foundation s broader strategy prioritises climate solutions and access to health, while its entrepreneurial programmes support early-, seed-, and growth-stage solutions with the aim of helping them move towards sustainable, revenue-based business models. Shine is particularly valuable because participating entrepreneurs can gain access not only to financial support but also to the expertise and networks associated with Swiss Re. For the 2027 edition, the programme also identifies Climate KIC as an ecosystem partner. The partnership is intended to strengthen connections within the wider climate innovation ecosystem and support solutions capable of addressing climate challenges at the city level. What Does Shine 2027 Offer? Shine 2027 is structured to provide more than conventional grant funding. The programme combines financial support with technical, strategic, and leadership assistance designed to help early-stage ventures become more resilient and scalable. Selected entrepreneurs can benefit from the following: 1. Swiss Re Expertise Participants can gain access to Swiss Re expertise in areas including the following: Risk Strategy Business development Business planning Market development Organisational resilience This expertise is intended to help entrepreneurs better understand risks and opportunities as they develop their ventures. 2. Leadership and Executive Coaching The programme provides leadership and executive coaching designed to help founders develop a stronger growth mindset. For an early-stage enterprise, founder capacity can be just as important as the underlying technology or solution. Shine, therefore, seeks to help entrepreneurs strengthen their leadership capabilities while preparing their organisations for growth. 3. Support for Scalable Climate Business Models Selected ventures receive support in developing business models that can grow beyond an initial pilot. The programme places considerable emphasis on financial sustainability and encourages applicants to pursue non-grant revenue streams and develop strong customer pipelines. 4. Grant Funding Shine includes grant funding intended to accelerate the validation and growth of participating ventures. The programme structure indicates an initial grant of up to USD 5,000 , with the remaining grant disbursed following a successful pitch co-created with Swiss Re colleagues. The programme also envisages a possible second round of investment of up to USD 300,000 for ventures that demonstrate sufficient scale. This reassessment is scheduled for January 2029 under the indicative programme timeline. 5. Ecosystem Connections Participants can gain access to ecosystem partners and climate innovation networks. These connections can be particularly valuable for entrepreneurs seeking: Strategic partnerships Investors Technical expertise Market opportunities Pilot opportunities Customers Additional sources of financing 6. Potential Follow-On Support Shine does not necessarily end when the four-month programme concludes. The Foundation indicates that participating ventures may subsequently gain access to mission-aligned investors, strategic ecosystem connections, potential pilot and market-access opportunities, and technical assistance. The Foundation may also consider reinvestment with a larger mandate after evidence of scale has been demonstrated. What Types of Climate Solutions Are Shine 2027 Looking For? Shine for Cities is focused on practical innovations addressing urban climate challenges. The 2027 programme identifies six major focus areas. 1. Energy Transition The programme is interested in solutions that accelerate the transition towards cleaner and lower-carbon energy systems. Examples include: Renewable energy adoption Distributed energy systems Energy storage Low-carbon energy access Technologies that enable cities and communities to reduce dependence on high-emission energy sources Entrepreneurs developing affordable and scalable clean-energy solutions may therefore find a strong alignment with this thematic area. 2. Building Efficiency and Electrification Buildings are a significant component of urban energy consumption and emissions. Shine is looking for innovations that can improve building energy performance and support the transition towards cleaner systems. Potential areas include: Energy-efficient buildings Building retrofits Electrification Energy management Technologies that reduce emissions from the built environment Solutions should demonstrate a clear pathway towards measurable climate impact. 3. Sustainable Transport Urban transportation is another important source of emissions and a major area for climate innovation. Shine identifies sustainable transport solutions such as the following: Low-carbon mobility Public transportation Active mobility Fleet electrification Equitable transport access Entrepreneurs developing solutions that make urban mobility cleaner, more efficient, and accessible may be particularly relevant to this category. 4. Waste and Circular Economy Shine also seeks innovations that address waste generation and resource use. Relevant solutions may include: Waste reduction Resource recovery Recycling systems Circular business models Technologies that divert waste from landfill Circular value chains The focus is not simply on waste management but on developing models capable of creating environmental and economic value. 5. Urban Nature and Land Use Nature-based approaches are another important component of the programme. Shine identifies solutions related to: Urban biodiversity Green infrastructure Sustainable food systems Nature-positive urban development Sustainable land use These approaches can contribute to climate resilience while also improving the quality and sustainability of urban environments. 6. Climate Data, Governance, and Monitoring The programme also recognises the importance of data and effective governance in delivering climate action. Innovations in this area may include: Climate intelligence platforms Climate decision-support tools Emissions tracking systems Climate-risk assessment tools Monitoring technologies Public engagement platforms Solutions that help cities understand climate risks, monitor progress, and make better decisions can therefore fit within this focus area. Who Should Apply for Shine 2027? Shine 2027 is designed for early-stage enterprises rather than individuals applying with only an idea . The official programme brochure identifies several important eligibility characteristics. Geographic Eligibility Applicants should be entrepreneurs operating in or serving one of the eight Shine cities . The eight participating city chapters are: Bangalore, India Bratislava, Slovakia Cape Town, South Africa London, United Kingdom Manila, Philippines Mexico City, Mexico New York, United States Zurich, Switzerland This means the opportunity is international in scope, but it is not an unrestricted global application programme . The venture must have a connection to one of the eight designated Shine cities. Stage of the Enterprise Applicants must be early-stage enterprises between 0 and 4 years of existence . Importantly, the venture should already have: A minimum viable product (MVP) A pilot underway, or A commercial launch underway Applicants whose ventures are still purely conceptual and have not developed an MVP may therefore not meet the programme s stated maturity requirement. Product or Service Innovation The innovation may be either: Product-based, or Service-based The solution should have the potential to contribute to emissions reduction and/or address climate adaptation and climate justice considerations. Scalable Business Model Applicants should demonstrate that their enterprise has a business model capable of achieving measurable environmental outcomes. The programme is particularly interested in ventures that can move beyond dependence on grants and establish sustainable revenue models. Applicants are therefore expected to demonstrate: A clear business model Potential for scalability Customer development A credible customer pipeline A pathway towards financial sustainability Climate Understanding Applicants should have a nuanced understanding of the environmental challenge their venture is addressing. They should also have a theory of change explaining how their solution is expected to produce meaningful environmental and social outcomes. Inclusion and Climate Justice Shine places importance on solutions that can make climate action more affordable and accessible to low-income communities. Where this focus is less directly applicable in a particular geography, the solution should nevertheless address climate mitigation or adaptation through a climate justice lens . This makes social inclusion an important consideration alongside environmental impact. Founder Commitment Founders selected for the programme must be prepared to commit significant time and attention during the four-month programme. The programme includes approximately 11 in-person days , with the remaining engagement taking place virtually. What Environmental and Social Impact Should Applicants Demonstrate? Shine is not simply looking for businesses that describe themselves as environmentally friendly. Applicants should be able to demonstrate how their solutions can generate measurable climate and social outcomes. The programme s primary environmental impact metric is Tonnes of CO₂ emissions avoided or reduced Depending on the nature of the venture, additional environmental indicators may include: Vulnerable land protected or restored Waste diverted from landfill Other measurable environmental improvements The Foundation also places emphasis on social impact. Examples of positive social outcomes include: Creating quality jobs and livelihood opportunities for low-income communities Increasing access to affordable climate solutions for underserved populations Improving quality of life through cleaner and healthier urban environments Improving urban resilience Expanding public access to climate information and awareness Helping individuals and communities adopt lower-emission behaviours and practices Shine 2027 Funding by City The programme operates through eight city chapters, with funding denominated according to the relevant local or programme currency. The indicative funding allocations listed in the official 2027 brochure are: Shine City Country Grant Amount Bangalore India INR 2,000,000 Bratislava Slovakia EUR 40,000 Cape Town South Africa ZAR 300,000 London United Kingdom GBP 40,000 Manila Philippines USD 30,000 Mexico City Mexico USD 30,000 New York United States USD 40,000 Zurich Switzerland CHF 55,000 These amounts are based on the August 2026 official Shine 2027 brochure. How Does the Shine 2027 Programme Work? The programme is structured as a four-month journey combining practical business development, impact management, leadership development, and interaction with Swiss Re colleagues. The three core modules are designed around different aspects of venture development. Module 1: Understanding the System and Business Strategy The first module focuses on helping entrepreneurs: Think in systems Connect with stakeholders Understand and decode business strategy This stage is important because urban climate challenges are interconnected. A successful climate solution needs to understand not only the technology but also the wider system in which it operates. Module 2: Designing for Impact and Market Readiness The second module focuses on: Designing for impact Developing an impact narrative Sharpening the go-to-market strategy Entrepreneurs can therefore work on translating their climate impact into a compelling and measurable proposition while strengthening their approach to customers and markets. Module 3: Resilience, Pitching and Leadership The third module focuses on: Building organisational resilience Preparing the business and implementation roadmap Pitching the business Developing emerging leadership capabilities The programme is therefore intended to leave entrepreneurs better prepared to execute their growth strategies rather than simply providing short-term financial assistance. Indicative Shine 2027 Timeline According to the official programme brochure, the Shine 2027 application and programme process is expected to follow the timeline below. August to September 2026 Applications for Shine 2027 open from approximately mid-August to mid-September 2026. 15 September 2026 The official brochure identifies 15 September 2026 as the application deadline. Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. Mid-September to Early November 2026 The Foundation expects to conduct due diligence and shortlist one enterprise for each chapter. Early November 2026 The initial grant of up to USD 5,000 is scheduled for disbursement. January to May 2027 The main Shine programme modules are scheduled to take place during this period. June 2027 The remaining grant is expected to be disbursed following a successful pitch co-created with Swiss Re colleagues. Connect Climate Impact With Inclusion A strong application should demonstrate how the solution can benefit communities that may otherwise be excluded from climate innovation. Show How the Venture Can Scale Shine is designed for entrepreneurs with solutions that can move beyond small pilots. Applicants should therefore explain: Where they are currently operating What the current market looks like Who the customers are What barriers to expansion exist What partnerships are required How additional funding would accelerate growth What measurable outcomes could be achieved at scale Why Shine 2027 Is Significant for Urban Climate Entrepreneurs Urban climate innovation is increasingly important because cities concentrate people, economic activity, infrastructure, and environmental pressures. A successful climate venture can therefore potentially generate significant impact by addressing problems in areas such as transport, energy, buildings, waste, urban nature, and climate information. Shine s approach is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs who need more than capital. Early-stage ventures often face challenges involving business strategy, market access, risk management, leadership, impact measurement, and partnerships. title: WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award 2026–2027: Win $5,000 to Advance Your Environmental and Conservation Leadership
summary: Young environmental leaders are increasingly playing a central role in responding to some of the world s most urgent environmental challenges. From protecting wildlife and restoring habitats to addressing climate change, reducing food waste and strengthening community resilience, youth-led initiatives are demonstrating that meaningful conservation action can begin at the community level. The WWF-US Youth Conservation Leadership Award 2026–2027 provides an important opportunity for an exceptional young conservation leader in the United States to receive recognition and financial support for their environmental leadership. Organized by World Wildlife Fund-US (WWF-US), the award celebrates young people who are developing and implementing conservation solutions and making outstanding contributions to environmental protection within their communities. Applications for the 2026–2027 cycle are currently being promoted through the official WWF-US website. About the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award The WWF-US Youth Conservation Leadership Award was established to recognize the achievements of exceptional young people working toward conservation solutions in the United States. Rather than focusing exclusively on academic achievement, the award highlights young leaders who are translating environmental concern into meaningful action. WWF-US particularly recognizes individuals whose leadership demonstrates how young people can contribute to addressing environmental challenges while inspiring others to become involved in conservation within their own communities. The award therefore provides more than recognition. It represents an opportunity for a promising conservation leader to strengthen their knowledge, professional capabilities and future contribution to environmental action. What Does the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award Recognize? The award recognizes youth leaders who are making outstanding contributions to environmental protection through community leadership, advocacy, research, conservation projects, education, innovation or other forms of environmental action. WWF identifies a broad range of environmental areas that may be relevant to the award, including: Climate change and efforts to address its impacts Community resilience in response to environmental challenges Biodiversity conservation Wildlife conservation Habitat protection and restoration Food waste reduction Environmental sustainability Community-based conservation Environmental advocacy and leadership Innovative responses to threats facing nature and communities This broad scope means that applicants do not necessarily need to work exclusively in traditional wildlife conservation. Young leaders working at the intersection of communities, climate, biodiversity, food systems, education, environmental justice, policy or sustainable development may also have relevant experience, provided their work demonstrates a meaningful contribution to conservation. US$5,000 Award for Conservation Leadership One of the major benefits of the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award is financial support for the selected conservation leader. The recipient may receive US$5,000 . Importantly, WWF explains that this funding is intended to support the winner s academic and/or professional development related to their conservation work . This creates opportunities for the recipient to strengthen the skills, expertise and professional capabilities needed to expand their environmental impact. Depending on the circumstances and applicable award requirements, professional or academic development could potentially help a conservation leader deepen their expertise, strengthen their leadership capacity or pursue further development connected with their environmental work. Applicants should therefore consider not only what they have already achieved but also how further academic or professional development could strengthen their future contribution to conservation. Who Is WWF Looking For? At the heart of the award is a simple question: is a young leader creating exceptional value for the movement to protect the planet? WWF is interested in young people who have moved beyond awareness and are demonstrating actual leadership. Competitive candidates are therefore likely to be individuals who can clearly demonstrate: Environmental commitment Their work addresses a genuine environmental or conservation challenge. Leadership They have played a meaningful role in initiating, leading, coordinating or expanding environmental action. Community involvement Their conservation work engages, supports or creates value for communities. Demonstrable impact Their work has generated, or has strong potential to generate, meaningful environmental outcomes. Innovation or problem-solving Their initiative introduces new approaches, partnerships, strategies or pathways for responding to environmental threats. Potential for continued leadership Their achievements demonstrate the capacity to continue contributing to conservation over the longer term. Conservation Areas That May Be Relevant WWF specifically highlights several environmental challenges when describing the award. Climate Change Young people working on climate mitigation, adaptation, climate education, policy advocacy or community-level climate action may find their work aligned with the award. Projects that help communities understand and respond to climate risks can be particularly relevant where they demonstrate tangible leadership and measurable impact. Community Resilience Environmental problems frequently affect communities directly through extreme weather, ecosystem degradation, pollution and other environmental pressures. Young leaders helping communities become more resilient to these challenges represent another important area recognized by WWF. Biodiversity Conservation Projects protecting species, ecosystems and ecological diversity may strongly align with WWF s conservation mission. Relevant initiatives may involve biodiversity research, restoration, education, advocacy, citizen science or community-based conservation. Wildlife Conservation Wildlife conservation remains an important part of WWF s global mission. Young scientists, conservationists, educators, organizers and community leaders contributing to the protection of wildlife may therefore have relevant experience for the award. Food Waste WWF explicitly includes food waste among the environmental issues represented by the award. Young leaders developing solutions to reduce food waste, improve resource efficiency, promote sustainable consumption or strengthen circular approaches to food systems may therefore fall within the award s broad conservation scope. Habitat Protection Healthy habitats are essential for biodiversity, wildlife and resilient ecosystems. Initiatives involving habitat restoration, land conservation, ecosystem protection and community stewardship can consequently demonstrate strong alignment with the objectives of the award. Why Community Leadership Matters A particularly important feature of the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award is its emphasis on community-level leadership. Environmental leadership does not necessarily require creating a large national organization. A young person can generate substantial impact by identifying an environmental problem affecting a particular community and mobilizing people, institutions and resources to address it. Strong community conservation projects may demonstrate qualities such as: Local participation Collaboration with stakeholders Environmental education Youth mobilization Evidence-based decision-making Practical environmental interventions Advocacy for environmental policies Community ownership Measurable environmental results Potential for replication or expansion WWF s approach recognizes that solutions to global environmental challenges frequently emerge through sustained local action. Examples of Previous WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award Winners Understanding previous recipients provides useful insight into the breadth of leadership recognized by WWF. Emmy Scott – 2025 Emmy Scott was selected as the 2025 recipient of the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award. Scott is a climate justice leader and Executive Director of Earth Guardians, an organization involving a global network of youth-led groups. Their work focuses on empowering young people to develop and lead community-driven conservation and climate solutions. The selection illustrates WWF s interest in leadership that combines grassroots engagement, youth empowerment and practical environmental action. Peter Pham – 2024 Peter Pham, a climate activist, environmental leader, policymaker and public servant, received the award in 2024. His environmental work included youth climate organizing, advocacy for climate legislation, public service and contributions to research addressing microplastic pollution. His background demonstrates that environmental leadership can combine policy, science, civic participation and grassroots advocacy. Charitie Ropati – 2023 Charitie Ropati is an Indigenous environmental and education activist, researcher and advocate whose work connects plant ecology, permafrost, cultural resilience and Indigenous communities. Her leadership demonstrates how conservation can intersect with scientific research, education, Indigenous knowledge and community resilience. Alexia Leclercq – 2022 Alexia Leclercq has worked as a grassroots organizer, educator, scholar and environmental justice advocate. Her work has included environmental campaigns addressing clean water, pollution, climate and environmental justice. Her selection illustrates the importance of community organizing and environmental justice within contemporary conservation leadership. Jasmin Graham – 2021 Jasmin Graham is a shark scientist and environmental educator whose work encompasses marine science, conservation, education, science communication and social justice. Her work also promotes greater representation within marine science. Alexa White – 2020 Alexa White s work connects agroecology, sustainable agriculture, environmental justice, biodiversity, food systems and international climate governance. Her background demonstrates how environmental research and sustainable food systems can contribute to conservation leadership. What Can Applicants Learn From Previous Winners? The backgrounds of previous recipients reveal an important characteristic of the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award: there is no single pathway to becoming a conservation leader. Previous winners have worked as: Climate activists Scientists Researchers Environmental educators Community organizers Policymakers Public servants Environmental justice advocates Youth leaders Nonprofit leaders The common denominator is meaningful environmental leadership. Applicants should therefore focus on explaining the environmental problem they are addressing, the role they personally played, the communities involved, the results achieved and how their work can contribute to broader conservation objectives. How to Prepare a Strong Application Candidates should carefully review the current application requirements before submitting their information. When preparing an application, it may be useful to clearly communicate the following elements. 1. Define the Environmental Problem Explain the conservation or environmental challenge being addressed. Avoid relying entirely on broad descriptions such as climate change is a major problem. Instead, demonstrate how the problem affects a specific ecosystem, species, population or community. 2. Explain Your Personal Leadership Role Applicants should clearly distinguish their own contribution from the work of their organization or team. Describe what you personally initiated, managed, developed, advocated, researched or implemented. 3. Demonstrate Impact Where possible, use evidence. Depending on the project, this could include: Number of people engaged Area of habitat restored or protected Amount of waste prevented or recovered Number of conservation activities conducted Policy changes achieved Communities reached Students or young people trained Species or ecosystems supported Partnerships established Research or advocacy outcomes Quantifiable results can make the scale of an applicant s contribution easier to understand. 4. Explain the Community Dimension Because the award emphasizes youth leadership within communities, applicants should demonstrate how local people or stakeholders participate in or benefit from their work. 5. Show Innovation If the initiative has developed a new conservation model, technology, partnership, campaign or approach, explain what makes it distinctive. 6. Explain Future Potential The award is not simply about recognizing past accomplishments. Applicants should also demonstrate how continued professional or academic development could strengthen their future contribution to conservation. Why the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award Matters Young environmental leaders often have ambitious ideas but limited access to funding, professional development and institutional visibility. Recognition from an internationally known conservation organization can help strengthen the profile of promising young conservationists while encouraging continued environmental leadership. The US$5,000 award can support the recipient s academic or professional development connected with conservation, potentially helping the winner acquire additional knowledge and capabilities needed to advance their work. Just as importantly, the initiative highlights youth leadership as an essential component of environmental problem-solving. Application Period for 2026–2027 WWF-US is currently promoting applications for the 2026–2027 WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award through its official website. The main WWF award page currently displays an Apply now for 2026–2027 application link. Applicants should carefully check the official application form for the current closing date and complete eligibility conditions before submitting, as the public-facing WWF award page does not presently display a specific application deadline. Interested candidates are encouraged to prepare their application materials promptly rather than waiting until the end of the application period. How to Apply Applications should be submitted through the official application route provided by WWF-US. Applicants should: Visit the official WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award webpage. Review the current 2026–2027 information. Select the official application option. Carefully review all eligibility requirements and instructions presented in the application form. Prepare accurate information about conservation achievements and leadership experience. Clearly demonstrate the environmental and community impact of the work. Complete all required application questions. Review the application carefully before submitting it. Applicants should rely on the official WWF-US application materials for final eligibility, deadline and submission requirements. Official Application Information The current opportunity and application access are available through the official World Wildlife Fund-US website: WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award: https://www.worldwildlife.org/support/advocacy/wwf-youth-conservation-leadership-award/ The page currently provides access to the 2026–2027 application. Conclusion The WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award 2026–2027 is an important recognition opportunity for young environmental leaders working to create meaningful conservation impact in the United States. With a US$5,000 award for academic and/or professional development , the initiative can help an outstanding young conservationist strengthen the skills and knowledge needed to expand their environmental contribution. From climate action and biodiversity conservation to wildlife protection, food waste reduction, environmental justice, habitat protection and community resilience, the award recognizes the increasingly diverse ways in which young people are responding to environmental challenges. Candidates who can demonstrate genuine leadership, measurable impact, strong community engagement and a clear commitment to protecting the planet should review the official WWF-US application requirements and consider applying. For young conservation leaders already turning environmental ideas into practical action, the WWF Youth Conservation Leadership Award provides an opportunity to have that work recognized and to build the capacity needed for even greater impact. title: Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships 2026: Win Up to $10,000 for STEM Study at a U.S. College or University
summary: Applications are now open for the Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships 2026 , an annual scholarship programme designed to recognize and support outstanding women pursuing education in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Through the Endeavour Women in Tech initiative, Endeavour Infrastructure aims to help address the continued underrepresentation of women across STEM fields while supporting students who have already demonstrated exceptional academic performance, research ability, technical achievement, or advocacy related to science and technology. For the 2026 cycle, selected recipients may receive scholarship awards of up to $10,000 to support their education. The opportunity is open to both: Women graduating from high school and entering their first year of college in fall 2026 Current undergraduate and graduate students attending a U.S. college or university Applicants must have a minimum 3.5 GPA and demonstrate exceptional work, research, and/or advocacy in STEM. The application deadline is September 8, 2026 . About the Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships The Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships , often associated with the Endeavour Women in Tech initiative, were created to recognize talented women pursuing STEM education and encourage their continued advancement in technology, engineering, science, mathematics, and related fields. Endeavour Infrastructure describes the scholarship programme as part of its wider commitment to supporting, advancing, and empowering women in technology and infrastructure. The programme is built around a simple reality: although women continue to make major contributions to innovation and scientific progress, they remain underrepresented in many STEM disciplines. The scholarship therefore seeks to identify students who are not only succeeding academically but also demonstrating meaningful engagement in their chosen STEM areas. This could include significant: Academic work Research Technical projects STEM advocacy Leadership Innovation Community engagement related to STEM Scholarship Value Each year, Endeavour awards scholarships of: Up to $10,000 per recipient Applicants should note that the exact amount may vary between recipients. For example, previous recipients have received awards of: $10,000 $5,000 $3,000 $2,000 The 2026 programme states that outstanding women pursuing STEM degrees can receive up to $10,000 . Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarship Impact Since the programme s development, Endeavour Women in Tech has provided significant support to students pursuing science and technology education. The programme reports that it has: Awarded more than $85,000 Supported 15 scholarship recipients Reached students across 12 universities Been operating since 2022 These figures demonstrate the growing reach of the programme and its continued commitment to supporting women entering or progressing through STEM education. Current University and Graduate Students Women who are already studying at a U.S. college or university may also apply. Minimum GPA Requirement Applicants must have a minimum: 3.5 GPA This is an important eligibility requirement. Candidates should therefore ensure that their current academic record meets or exceeds this threshold before submitting an application. The scholarship is competitive, so applicants with strong grades should also focus on demonstrating how their STEM experience extends beyond academic performance alone. Eligible STEM Fields The scholarship is intended for women pursuing education in: Science Technology Engineering Mathematics The supplied programme information does not provide a complete list of eligible majors. However, STEM programmes may potentially include areas such as: Science Students may be studying disciplines connected to the natural or applied sciences. Technology Technology-related majors may include areas connected to computing, information systems, software, emerging technologies, or other technical fields. Engineering Engineering applicants may come from a range of engineering disciplines. Mathematics Students pursuing mathematics or strongly quantitative programmes may also be relevant. Exceptional STEM Work Applicants may be able to demonstrate their abilities through substantial academic, technical, or practical work. Examples might include: STEM projects Technical competitions Engineering design work Programming projects Scientific initiatives Academic projects Innovation-related activities Applicants should focus on explaining what they personally contributed and what they learned or achieved. Research Experience Research is specifically highlighted by Endeavour as one of the areas that may strengthen an application. Research experience could potentially include: Laboratory research University research projects Independent research Faculty-assisted projects Research internships Conference presentations Scientific publications Technical investigations A candidate should clearly communicate the purpose of the research, their role, and any outcomes generated. STEM Advocacy The scholarship also welcomes applicants who have demonstrated advocacy in STEM. Advocacy could involve work intended to: Encourage girls to pursue STEM Improve access to science and technology education Support women in technical careers Promote STEM learning in underserved communities Mentor younger students Organize science or technology programmes Support diversity and inclusion within STEM This element makes the scholarship particularly interesting because applicants do not necessarily need to rely entirely on research achievements. Leadership and community impact may also strengthen the application. Why Women in STEM Matter The Endeavour Women in Tech initiative is grounded in the recognition that women remain underrepresented in many areas of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Supporting women in STEM can have effects far beyond individual scholarships. Increasing the participation of women can contribute to: More diverse research teams Broader perspectives in technology development Greater representation in engineering More inclusive innovation Stronger pathways for future women scientists and technologists More diverse leadership across technology and infrastructure Financial support can also reduce barriers that make it difficult for talented students to continue developing their education. The scholarship therefore combines financial assistance with recognition of women already demonstrating excellence and promise in STEM. Past Scholarship Recipients Previous Endeavour Women in Tech scholarship recipients have attended several prominent universities. Past awardees have studied at institutions including: Colorado School of Mines Massachusetts Institute of Technology University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign San Jose State University University of Maryland University of Colorado Boulder Stanford University Villanova University Columbia University Cornell University University of Alabama Howard University Award amounts have varied depending on the year and recipient. Some previous students received the maximum $10,000, while others received smaller awards. This reinforces the importance of describing the programme accurately as offering up to $10,000 , rather than assuming every selected student receives the maximum amount. Application Categories Endeavour provides separate application pathways for: Incoming University Students This application is intended for students graduating from high school and beginning their first year of university. APPLY HERE Current University Students This route is designed for students who are currently enrolled in college or graduate study. APPLY HERE Applicants should use the application link corresponding to their current educational status. How to Prepare a Strong Application Because the scholarship recognizes exceptional STEM achievement, candidates should prepare an application that goes beyond simply listing grades and activities. 1. Check Your GPA Make sure your academic record demonstrates the required minimum: 3.5 GPA Applicants below the stated threshold would not meet the published eligibility criteria. Application Deadline Applications for the 2026 Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships close on: September 8, 2026 Applicants should submit before the deadline wherever possible. Waiting until the final hours can create unnecessary risk if technical difficulties, missing materials, or application errors arise. For an incoming college student, the scholarship can provide meaningful financial support at the beginning of a STEM degree. For an undergraduate or graduate student, it can provide recognition for research, technical achievement, or advocacy already underway. Applicants who have strong academic performance and a clear record of STEM engagement should therefore seriously consider submitting an application. Conclusion The Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships 2026 offer an important opportunity for women pursuing science, technology, engineering, and mathematics at colleges and universities in the United States. Selected recipients may receive up to $10,000 , helping support their continued academic and professional development. The scholarship is open to women graduating from high school and entering college in fall 2026, as well as current undergraduate and graduate students studying at U.S. institutions. title: WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey: Fully Funded Leadership Programme for Women in Health

Participants therefore explore both personal leadership development and systems-level health challenges . What Makes the 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey Different? The programme combines several complementary elements rather than relying on traditional classroom-based training. Participants will have access to: Intensive leadership learning Virtual learning touchpoints Group mentoring Individual executive coaching Leadership assessments In-person experiential learning A Health Leadership Project A diverse regional network of women leaders Opportunities to collaborate across sectors Continued engagement through a lifelong community This combination is intended to help participants translate leadership concepts into practical action.
