Across the programme, the estimated total learning commitment is approximately 87 hours , including learning touchpoints and work associated with the Health Leadership Project. The hybrid structure allows participants to remain engaged with their professional responsibilities while participating in carefully designed leadership-development experiences. However, participants should understand that the required sessions are considered important components of the programme and that attendance is expected. Cost: A Fully Funded Leadership Opportunity One of the most significant advantages of the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey is that it is offered free of charge to selected participants . WomenLift Health states that programme costs are covered, including: Programme participation Travel associated with required in-person experiences Lodging associated with those experiences This funding structure is intended to make the leadership-development experience accessible to qualified women leaders without requiring participants to personally finance the programme s major participation costs. Because the programme involves live, interactive learning and in-person residencies, selected participants are expected to make the necessary time available for participation. Who Is the Programme Designed For? The Southern Africa Leadership Journey is designed for mid-career women leaders working in health and related sectors . WomenLift Health takes a broad view of what constitutes health leadership. Rather than limiting participation to physicians, nurses or public health professionals, the programme recognises that sustainable health improvements depend on action across multiple interconnected areas. Participants may therefore come from different professional sectors and disciplines that influence health outcomes. These can include: Public health Healthcare Medicine Nursing Health policy Education Agriculture Food systems Climate Water and sanitation Technology Gender equity Economic policy Non-governmental organisations Academia Philanthropy Private-sector organisations Public-sector institutions The programme calls this broader approach Health++ . Understanding the Health++ Concept WomenLift Health defines Health++ as the recognition that sustainable improvements in health require coordinated action across interconnected fields that shape and enable health. These include areas such as: Climate change Food systems Agriculture Water and sanitation Education Economic policy Gender equity Technology The Health++ approach is based on the understanding that health challenges cannot always be solved within the boundaries of the health sector alone. For example, health outcomes can be influenced by whether people have access to nutritious food, clean water, safe environments, education, economic opportunities, technology and equitable services. The Leadership Journey therefore seeks leaders who can think beyond professional silos and work across interconnected systems. Why Health++ Matters The programme identifies several important relationships between health and other sectors. Health and Climate Climate change can influence disease patterns, nutrition, environmental conditions and people s ability to access healthcare. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events and pollution can create additional health risks and increase pressure on health systems. Women leaders working at the intersection of climate and health can therefore contribute to solutions that address both environmental and health challenges. Health and Agriculture Agriculture and food systems have direct implications for nutrition, livelihoods and health. Food systems can influence problems ranging from malnutrition to obesity while also affecting rural communities and economies. Cross-sectoral leadership can help address these challenges more effectively. Health and Gender Gender influences access to healthcare, health decision-making and leadership. Understanding power dynamics and gender-related barriers is therefore important for developing health systems that are more equitable. Women leaders can play a significant role in identifying and addressing these structural challenges. Health and Technology Technology is increasingly changing healthcare delivery, diagnostics and access to services. Digital health tools can create new opportunities while also raising questions about accessibility, equity and inclusion. Leaders who understand both health systems and technology can help ensure innovation contributes to better and more equitable outcomes. Developing Women Leaders Across Health++ The programme seeks to develop leaders who can: Collaborate across sectors Think beyond traditional professional boundaries Build coalitions Understand complex systems Identify catalytic leverage points Influence institutions Strengthen their leadership presence Create sustainable health impact This approach is intended to prepare women leaders to address complex problems that require cooperation between multiple sectors and stakeholders. Core Elements of the WomenLift Health Leadership Journey The programme consists of several interconnected components. 1. Health Leadership Project The Health Leadership Project (HLP) is a central component of the Journey. Participants enter the programme with an idea for a project that addresses a health-related challenge. The project gives each participant an opportunity to design and lead an initiative that draws upon their: Expertise Professional network Passion Creativity Leadership capabilities The goal is to turn leadership learning into practical health impact. Developing the Health Leadership Project Participants work on several components of their project, including: A Theory of Change Stakeholder constellation mapping An implementation plan They receive guidance from: A mentor An HLP reviewer Global health experts within the WomenLift Health team and network The implementation phase begins during the latter part of the Leadership Journey. Participants present their project s development and early outcomes during the Lift-Off event. The project does not have to be fully completed by the end of the Journey. Participants are expected to continue implementation beyond the programme where appropriate. Three Principles for the Health Leadership Project WomenLift Health identifies three major guidelines for HLP projects. 1. Improve Health Outcomes Projects should focus on improving health outcomes and incorporate gender considerations into interventions, policies and systems. Participants should consider differences in: Health burdens Risks Access to care Experiences Outcomes 2. Strengthen Leadership The project should provide an opportunity for participants to apply and strengthen their leadership capabilities. Participants are encouraged to balance: Personal control Influence Collaboration Resource mobilisation Sustainable impact 3. Address Health Challenges Through a Systems Lens Participants should channel their passion into addressing a public health challenge while considering: Structures Policies Stakeholders Root causes Systems Long-term sustainability Scalability This approach is designed to move projects beyond short-term interventions toward sustainable change. 2. Learning Touchpoints Learning Touchpoints are facilitated virtual and in-person group sessions. They use interactive and workshop-style approaches rather than relying exclusively on lectures. Participants explore: Leadership frameworks Leadership research Practical leadership tools Personal development Professional growth Health leadership priorities Relevant sector issues Health Leadership Projects The sessions also create opportunities for participants to learn from one another. The cohort s diversity is therefore an important part of the learning experience. 3. Mentoring Touchpoints Participants will also receive group mentoring from experienced senior leaders. WomenLift Health identifies mentors from different: Professional backgrounds Health sectors Disciplines Career trajectories Mentoring groups consist of several cohort members and a mentor. Mentors are matched with participants based on complementary backgrounds, professional trajectories and, in some cases, Health Leadership Project topics. The mentor serves as a technical and career resource throughout the Journey. 4. One-on-One Executive Coaching Individual coaching is another major feature of the programme. Each participant is paired with an executive coach who works with her individually. The coaching relationship helps participants: Identify strengths Understand areas for development Navigate change Respond to new leadership challenges Strengthen leadership effectiveness Prepare for future leadership responsibilities Leadership-style assessments, including a 360-rater evaluation , are used to inform coaching conversations. This provides participants with structured feedback about their leadership capabilities and helps them identify areas they may wish to strengthen. The combination of mentoring and coaching gives participants both: A broader professional support network; and Personalised leadership-development guidance. 5. In-Person Leadership Immersion The Leadership Immersion is a three-day experiential learning event held several months into the Journey. The Immersion gives participants the opportunity to move beyond virtual learning and engage directly with their cohort. Activities include: Dynamic discussions Practical exercises Real-world leadership examples Reflection Peer learning Application of leadership concepts The 2027 programme schedule identifies the Immersion as taking place from 13–16 April 2027 , with travel days on 12 April and 17 April . The specific location will be communicated to selected cohort members closer to the event, but it will be somewhere in Southern Africa . 6. Leadership Lift-Off The Leadership Lift-Off takes place toward the end of the Journey. It is designed to celebrate the cohort s development and prepare participants for the next stage of their leadership journey. The programme describes both public and private Lift-Off experiences. Public Lift-Off Participants reflect on their leadership development throughout the year and present their Health Leadership Projects to: Fellow cohort members Other health audiences Relevant stakeholders Private Lift-Off The private Lift-Off is a two-day event focused on celebrating the cohort s growth and preparing participants for the next phase of their leadership. The programme information provided lists the Lift-Off as 14–15 March 2028 , with travel days on 13 March and 16 March . Applicants should carefully review the official programme calendar because the dates provided extend beyond the stated February 2026–March 2027 programme-duration description on the webpage. Lifelong Leadership Community Completing the Leadership Journey does not mark the end of participants relationship with WomenLift Health. Those who successfully complete the Journey become Global Fellows and join a lifelong network of women leaders. The network provides continuing opportunities for: Peer support Professional collaboration Regional networking Global networking Mentorship Leadership exchange Advocacy for women s leadership Participants therefore become part of a community that continues beyond the formal programme. Diversity, Inclusion and Representation Inclusion is a central value of WomenLift Health. The organisation states that transformative leadership should: Advocate for women Give women a voice Represent women with diverse lived experiences WomenLift Health encourages applications from: Minorities Historically marginalised communities Underrepresented communities within the countries served by the programme. The organisation also seeks diversity across: Sectors Disciplines Cultures Professional backgrounds Lived experiences This means the Southern Africa Leadership Journey is not designed around one narrow professional profile. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet all of the stated eligibility requirements. 1. Applicants Must Identify as Women The programme is specifically designed for women leaders. Applicants must identify as women to qualify for consideration. 2. English Fluency Applicants must demonstrate confidence and fluency in both written and verbal English . This is important because participants are expected to: Express emotions and personal experiences Participate in reflective conversations Engage in complex interpersonal discussions Understand and apply leadership-development concepts Participate actively in group sessions 3. Citizenship, Residence and Employment Applicants must be citizens who reside and work in one of the following countries: Angola Botswana Lesotho Malawi Mozambique Namibia South Africa eSwatini Zambia Zimbabwe Applicants outside these countries do not meet the stated country eligibility requirement for the 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey. 4. Time-Zone Requirement Applicants must live within CAT, plus or minus one hour , for at least 75% of the Leadership Journey . WomenLift Health considers time-zone compatibility essential because participants need to attend scheduled learning touchpoints and interact with their peers. 5. Professional Experience Applicants must be mid-career leaders with between 10 and 25 years of work experience in Health++. This requirement distinguishes the Leadership Journey from programmes aimed at students, recent graduates or early-career professionals. The programme is intended for experienced professionals who are ready to deepen their leadership influence. What Does 10–25 Years of Experience in Health++ Mean? The requirement should not necessarily be interpreted as requiring 10–25 years of work exclusively within hospitals, medical institutions or traditional public health organisations. WomenLift Health s Health++ definition is intentionally broad. Relevant professional experience can involve interconnected sectors such as: Climate Agriculture Food systems Water and sanitation Education Economic policy Gender Technology The important consideration is the relationship between the applicant s work and health impact. Professional Diversity Within the Cohort WomenLift Health intends to create a diverse cohort representing different sectors, including: Public sector Private sector Academia Non-governmental organisations Philanthropy This diversity is intended to strengthen cross-sector collaboration and expose participants to perspectives outside their immediate professional environments. Application Requirements A complete application must include a letter of recommendation . The preferred recommender is the applicant s supervisor. However, if an applicant cannot obtain a recommendation from her direct supervisor, she may submit a letter from: A senior leader within her current organisation; or A leader in the health community who has experience working with her. The letter should address the applicant s: Leadership Contributions The recommender should describe significant contributions the applicant has made to her professional field that demonstrate leadership capacity. Distinguishing Personal Qualities The recommendation should identify the applicant s strongest personal quality and explain how that quality distinguishes her as a candidate. Leadership Development Potential The recommender should explain how participation in the Leadership Journey could help the applicant strengthen her leadership knowledge and skills. The recommendation letter must be uploaded as part of the application by the application deadline for the application to be considered complete. The Health Leadership Project Is Particularly Important Applicants should pay close attention to the Health Leadership Project component when preparing their applications. WomenLift Health states that the project and its description carry significant weight in the application review process. Strong applicants are expected to demonstrate: Original thinking A clear mission Leadership potential Understanding of the health challenge Systems thinking Practical ambition Potential for meaningful health impact Applicants are therefore encouraged to review the official Health Leadership Project materials before beginning the application. Using Artificial Intelligence in the Application WomenLift Health acknowledges that applicants increasingly use artificial intelligence tools when preparing applications. The organisation does not prohibit thoughtful use of AI, but it emphasises that application responses should remain: Specific Contextualised Rooted in the applicant s actual work Connected to genuine interests Based on realistic goals Reflective of the applicant s own thinking Applicants should avoid submitting generic responses that could have been written for anyone. The organisation notes that vague responses or applications that appear substantially similar to those of other applicants may receive lower ratings in a highly competitive selection process. Applicants may therefore use technology as a support tool, but their application should demonstrate their own experience, ideas, leadership journey and goals. Participation Commitments and Expectations The Leadership Journey offers extensive support at no cost to participants, including: Mentoring Coaching Assessments Virtual learning In-person experiences Because the programme receives hundreds of applications and has limited places, selected participants are expected to take their commitment seriously. Accepting a place means agreeing to participate fully. The programme s virtual and in-person sessions are designed as live, small-group learning experiences. Each participant s presence contributes to the experience of the entire cohort. Participants should therefore plan their schedules carefully and make every reasonable effort to attend all required sessions. If an absence becomes unavoidable, participants are expected to inform WomenLift Health as soon as they know they cannot attend. Applicants should also review the official Terms of Acceptance covering attendance and data policies. Programme Schedule The programme includes several major learning milestones and touchpoints. Applicants should review the official calendar carefully before applying because participation in the required sessions is mandatory. The programme information states that participants should ensure they can attend all scheduled touchpoints and in-person residencies. The in-person components involve travel within Southern Africa. The published calendar identifies: Leadership Immersion 13–16 April 2027 Travel days: 12 April 2027 17 April 2027 Leadership Lift-Off 14–15 March 2028 Travel days: 13 March 2028 16 March 2028 The exact locations of the in-person residencies will be communicated to selected cohort members closer to the events and will be in Southern Africa. Why Apply to the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey? The programme provides an unusual combination of leadership development, professional networking, coaching, mentoring and practical health impact. Selected participants can benefit from: Leadership Development Participants gain frameworks and tools to strengthen their leadership effectiveness. Executive Coaching One-on-one coaching provides personalised support for understanding strengths and areas for growth. Mentorship Participants learn from experienced leaders working across different health sectors and disciplines. Peer Network The cohort provides a community of women leaders who can exchange knowledge, perspectives and professional experiences. Health Leadership Project Participants develop and lead a project addressing a real health challenge. Regional Exposure The programme brings together women leaders from across Southern Africa. Long-Term Community Successful participants become part of a lifelong WomenLift Health network. Fully Funded Participation The programme is free, with programme costs and required travel and lodging covered. How to Apply Interested applicants should first confirm that they meet every eligibility requirement. They should then review the programme s official resources, particularly: Leadership Journey Framework Health Leadership Project Guidelines Frequently Asked Questions Programme Calendar Terms of Acceptance Applicants should also identify an appropriate recommender and ensure that the recommendation letter can be submitted before the deadline. The official WomenLift Health application page should be used to submit the application. Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM CAT. APPLY HERE! Applicants with questions about eligibility can contact: southernafricajourney@WomenLifthealth.org Who Qualifies for the 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey? Category of eligible people The programme is designed for mid-career women leaders working in health and interconnected Health++ fields . Eligible applicants must: Identify as women. Have 10–25 years of work experience. Work in Health++ or an interconnected field affecting health. Be citizens of an eligible Southern African country. Reside and work in that eligible country. Demonstrate strong written and spoken English. Live within CAT, plus or minus one hour, for at least 75% of the programme. Be willing and able to participate fully in the programme. Submit the required recommendation letter. Eligible countries Applicants must be citizens who reside and work in: Angola Botswana Lesotho Malawi Mozambique Namibia South Africa eSwatini Zambia Zimbabwe Race, ethnicity and continental eligibility The programme does not specify a race or ethnicity restriction in the eligibility criteria provided. However, WomenLift Health explicitly encourages applications from minorities and historically marginalised and underrepresented communities in the countries it serves. Geographically, the programme is specifically targeted at Southern Africa , rather than being open to applicants from all African countries or all continents. Visit HERE to learn more about the WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey. Important Deadline The application deadline is: 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM Central Africa Time (CAT). Applicants should ensure that the complete application, including the required recommendation letter, is submitted before the deadline. Because the programme is highly competitive and places are limited, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to complete their application. APPLY HERE! Conclusion The WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey offers a comprehensive leadership-development opportunity for experienced women leaders seeking to increase their influence and create meaningful health impact across Southern Africa. The programme goes beyond conventional professional training by combining leadership education, mentoring, executive coaching, peer learning, experiential residencies and a practical Health Leadership Project. Participants are given the opportunity to reflect on their leadership journey, develop new skills, build influential relationships and apply their learning to a real-world health challenge. Its Health++ approach is particularly significant because it recognises that sustainable health improvements require collaboration across sectors such as climate change, agriculture, food systems, education, technology, gender equity, economic policy and water and sanitation. For eligible women with 10–25 years of professional experience , the programme provides an opportunity to strengthen leadership capabilities while joining a diverse network of women leaders from across Southern Africa. Participation is free , and programme costs, including required travel and lodging, are covered. However, selected participants must be prepared to make the necessary time commitment and attend the required virtual and in-person sessions. Women who are citizens, residents and workers in Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, eSwatini, Zambia or Zimbabwe , meet the professional-experience requirement, are confident in English and satisfy the time-zone requirement should consider applying. The application deadline is 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM CAT . Prospective applicants should carefully review the official programme calendar, eligibility requirements, Health Leadership Project guidelines and application instructions before submitting their applications. For women leaders ready to deepen their leadership influence, expand their regional network and translate their expertise into sustainable health impact, the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey offers a significant platform for professional and personal transformation. title: Jesus College Cambridge Research Fellowships 2027 | 3-Year Fellowships in UK
summary: Jesus College, University of Cambridge is inviting applications for three Research Fellowships for early-career researchers who are nearing completion of their PhD or have recently started their postdoctoral careers. The fellowships provide an opportunity to spend three years developing research within the academic environment of the University of Cambridge , with a starting remuneration of £32,882 , additional benefits and research support. Two of the fellowships are available across selected Arts and Humanities subjects , while one fellowship is available in the Sciences . About the Jesus College Research Fellowships The Research Fellowships are designed for researchers at the early stages of their academic careers. The fellowships are normally three years in duration and are expected to commence on 1 October 2027 . The opportunity is particularly suitable for candidates who are: Graduate students in the latter stages of research leading to a PhD; or Postdoctoral researchers who have recently been awarded their PhD. Jesus College notes that candidates who have undertaken more than five years of full-time research are unlikely to be considered . However, the College may consider exceptions where candidates are able to present a case explaining their circumstances as part of the application. Research Fellowship Areas Arts Research Fellowships Two Research Fellowships are available in the following subject areas: Anglo-Saxon, Norse and Celtic (ASNC) Education Studies English Law Modern Languages Theology Applicants should ensure that their proposed research fits clearly within one of the advertised subject areas. Science Research Fellowship A separate Research Fellowship is available in the Sciences . The Science fellowship provides an opportunity for an early-career researcher to develop their research within the Cambridge academic environment. Who Should Apply? The fellowships are intended for brilliant early-career researchers who are beginning to establish themselves as independent scholars. Applicants may be: Current PhD students who are approaching completion of their doctoral research. Researchers who have recently completed a PhD. Early-career postdoctoral researchers. Candidates who have undertaken more than five years of full-time research are generally unlikely to be considered, although exceptions may be possible. The College is looking for researchers who can demonstrate the importance and potential of their current and proposed research. Fellowship Benefits Successful candidates will receive several financial and academic benefits throughout the fellowship. £32,882 Starting Remuneration The remuneration for a Research Fellow is determined by reference to the University of Cambridge salary scale and starts at £32,882 . Three-Year Fellowship The fellowship provides funding and support for three years , normally commencing on 1 October 2027 . This gives early-career researchers valuable time to develop their research, publications and academic profile. Free Meals Research Fellows receive a free dinner or lunch at Jesus College, regardless of whether they live in College or elsewhere. Research Benefits Certain research-related expenses may be reimbursed, providing additional support for fellows undertaking their academic work. Pension Research Fellows may also be eligible to join the University Pension Scheme . Application Requirements Candidates will need to complete the application process through the Jesus College Research Fellowship application system. Applications must include the required information and supporting materials. Shortlisted candidates will subsequently be asked to provide: One sample of written work , up to a maximum of 40,000 words . A 500-word statement explaining the importance of their current and proposed research. Reports from two referees . Applicants should therefore begin preparing their research materials and contacting potential referees well ahead of the deadline. What Should Your Research Statement Demonstrate? The 500-word statement provides shortlisted candidates with an opportunity to explain why their research matters. Applicants should use this space to clearly communicate: The significance of their current research. The direction of their proposed research. Why the proposed work is important. How their research could contribute to their academic field. Their potential as an early-career researcher. A clear and focused research proposal can help demonstrate the intellectual value and future potential of the candidate s work. Application Timeline Applications Open: 3 August 2026 Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 Closing Time: 5:00 PM Fellowship Start Date: 1 October 2027 Duration: Three years Location: Jesus College, Cambridge, United Kingdom How to Apply Applications are submitted online through the Jesus College Research Fellowship application portal. Application Portal Apply through the Jesus College Research Fellowship Portal Applicants can also find additional information about the vacancies and fellowship opportunities on the College s official website. Jesus College Vacancies and Fellowships Important Information for Applicants Candidates should carefully review the official fellowship details before applying. In particular, applicants should consider their career stage. These fellowships are specifically intended for early-career researchers , and candidates with more than five years of full-time research are unlikely to be considered unless they can provide a convincing explanation for an exception. Shortlisted applicants should also be prepared to submit substantial written work of up to 40,000 words and a concise 500-word research statement . It is therefore advisable to prepare application materials well before the deadline and ensure that referees have sufficient time to submit their reports. Why Apply? The Jesus College Research Fellowships provide an opportunity for emerging researchers to develop their academic careers within one of the world s most recognised university environments. Beyond the financial remuneration, fellows can benefit from the College s academic community, research support and opportunities to interact with researchers across different disciplines. For researchers transitioning from doctoral study into independent research, a three-year fellowship can provide valuable time to strengthen their research portfolio, develop publications and establish themselves within their field. Conclusion The Jesus College Cambridge Research Fellowships 2027 offer three early-career researchers the opportunity to undertake supported research at Jesus College, University of Cambridge . With a starting remuneration of £32,882 , a three-year fellowship, research-related benefits, free College meals and potential access to the University Pension Scheme, the opportunity provides substantial support for researchers at the beginning of their academic careers. The fellowships are open across the Sciences, ASNC, Education Studies, English, Law, Modern Languages and Theology , making the opportunity relevant to researchers from a range of academic disciplines. If you are completing your PhD or have recently received your doctorate and are looking for an opportunity to develop your research in Cambridge, this fellowship is worth considering. Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 5:00 PM. Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage . title: 2027 Peter McMullin Centre Visiting Fellowship on Statelessness: Up to AUD 6,000 in Funding for International Researchers and Practitioners
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 Visiting Fellowship Scheme at the Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness , offering researchers, practitioners and educators an opportunity to spend time at the Centre, undertake research related to statelessness and develop international academic and professional collaborations. The funded fellowship provides up to AUD 6,000 to support international travel and accommodation costs in Melbourne. The fellowship is expected to last approximately one to two months and can be undertaken between August and October 2027 . The opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers and professionals working on statelessness, nationality, citizenship, displacement, migration, human rights, international law and related areas. 2027 Peter McMullin Centre Visiting Fellowship at a Glance Detail Information Host Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness Institution Melbourne Law School, University of Melbourne Opportunity Visiting Research Fellowship Year 2027 Funding Up to AUD 6,000 Duration Suggested 1–2 months Visit period August–October 2027 Location Melbourne, Australia Research area Statelessness and related issues Application deadline 30 November 2026 Application format One PDF document Visa/insurance International visitors are responsible for their own visa and insurance costs About the Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness The Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness is based at Melbourne Law School, University of Melbourne , and focuses on research, education and collaboration relating to statelessness. Its Visiting Fellowship Scheme provides an opportunity for people working on statelessness to engage directly with the Centre s work while developing research collaborations and international professional networks. The fellowship is designed not simply as a period of independent research, but as an opportunity for Visiting Fellows to become involved in the intellectual and professional activities of the Centre during their stay. What Does the Funded Fellowship Offer? The 2027 funded Visiting Fellowship provides financial assistance of up to AUD 6,000 . The funding can support: International travel to Melbourne Accommodation in Melbourne during the fellowship Other eligible costs associated with undertaking the visit, subject to the proposed budget Applicants must provide a detailed breakdown of the amount requested. If airfare is required, applicants should include the estimated airfare cost in their budget. The maximum amount available is AUD 6,000 . Fellowship Duration and Timing The suggested duration of the fellowship is one to two months . The funded fellowship is available to be undertaken between: August and October 2027. Applicants should therefore propose their preferred dates within this period as part of their application. What Will Visiting Fellows Do? Visiting Fellows are expected to participate actively in the life and work of the Peter McMullin Centre during their stay. This can include: Conducting research related to statelessness Developing research collaborations Participating in Centre events Attending workshops Engaging with researchers and other Centre members Sharing research ideas and expertise Contributing to discussions relevant to statelessness research The fellowship is therefore suitable for individuals who want more than simply access to a workspace while conducting independent research. Workspace and Research Facilities Visiting Fellows will be provided with a workspace during their stay. They will also have access to: Library facilities Computer facilities Centre activities Events and workshops These resources can support researchers in conducting their proposed research while being based in Melbourne. Research Presentation Requirement As part of the fellowship, Visiting Fellows are expected to share their research with the Centre and wider audiences. Depending on the nature of their work, fellows will present their research through: A Faculty seminar A public seminar A work-in-progress meeting This provides fellows with an opportunity to receive feedback, discuss their research with other academics and professionals, and contribute to intellectual exchange at the Centre. Contribution to the Critical Statelessness Studies Blog Visiting Fellows are also expected, where appropriate, to contribute a blog post to the Critical Statelessness Studies blog . This provides an additional opportunity to communicate research findings, ideas or insights to a broader audience interested in statelessness and related issues. Who Can Apply for the Fellowship? The Centre explicitly recognises that statelessness research and professional work are undertaken by people in different career stages and professional settings. Applications are welcomed from: Postdoctoral researchers Early-career researchers Established academics Tenured academics Statelessness practitioners Non-academic professionals Educators Researchers with lived experience of statelessness The Centre particularly states that researchers with lived experience of statelessness are strongly encouraged to apply . Non-Academic Applicants Are Also Eligible Importantly, the fellowship is not restricted to university academics. Non-academic visiting professionals can also be considered if they propose an applied research project that is relevant to the work of the Centre. This makes the opportunity potentially suitable for professionals working in areas such as: Human rights Refugee protection Migration Nationality and citizenship Legal practice Policy Advocacy International development Statelessness-related programmes The proposed project must demonstrate relevance to the Centre s work. What Must Be Included in the Application? Applications for the funded fellowship must be submitted as one PDF document containing the required materials. Applicants need to provide the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae and Publications List Applicants should include their CV along with a list of their publications. This allows the selection team to understand the applicant s academic, research or professional background and previous work. 2. Research Plan A research plan of no more than 1,000 words is required. The research plan should explain: The research the applicant intends to undertake The purpose and objectives of the research Proposed activities during the visit Potential collaborations How the applicant intends to contribute to the work of the Centre Applicants should demonstrate a clear connection between their proposed research and the Centre s focus on statelessness. 3. Proposed Fellowship Dates Applicants must indicate their proposed dates for the visit . For the funded 2027 fellowship, the visit should fall within the available August–October 2027 period. 4. Funding Request and Budget Applicants must state the amount of funding they are requesting, up to the maximum of: AUD 6,000 A detailed budget breakdown must accompany the request. Where international air travel is required, the budget should include the estimated cost of airfare. 5. Reference Letter Applicants must provide one letter of reference . For non-academic applicants, the Centre accepts a letter of support from an employer or another organisation or entity with which the applicant is professionally associated . How to Apply Applications should be submitted by email to: law-statelessness@unimelb.edu.au The email subject line should be: Visiting Fellowship Application Applicants should submit the complete application as one PDF document . Questions about the fellowship can also be directed to the same email address. Application Deadline The deadline for applications for the 2027 funded Visiting Fellowship is 30 November 2026 . Applicants should ensure that their complete application is submitted before the deadline. Important Information for International Applicants Applicants travelling to Australia from outside the country are responsible for obtaining and paying for any necessary: Australian visa Travel documentation Insurance These costs are separate from the fellowship funding arrangements and applicants should take them into account when planning their visit. Self-Funded Visiting Fellowship Option The Centre also welcomes applicants who are able to fund their own visit . Self-funded visitors can apply to visit the Centre throughout the year. Subject to availability, self-funded visitors may receive: Workspace Library access Computer access Opportunities to participate in Centre events Opportunities to participate in workshops Engagement with the Centre s academic and professional community Unlike the funded fellowship, self-funded visits do not have the 30 November 2026 deadline. Applications for self-funded visits can be made year-round . Requirements for Self-Funded Visitors Self-funded applicants should provide: Curriculum vitae and publications list Research plan of up to 1,000 words Proposed dates of the visit One letter of reference For non-academic visitors, the reference can be a letter of support from their employer or another professionally associated organisation. Funded vs Self-Funded Visit Feature Funded Fellowship Self-Funded Visit Funding Up to AUD 6,000 No Centre funding stated Research focus Statelessness-related research Relevant research Duration Suggested 1–2 months Proposed by visitor Visit period August–October 2027 Year-round applications Workspace Yes Subject to availability Library access Yes Yes Computer access Yes Yes Centre participation Expected Encouraged Research plan Required Required CV/publications Required Required Reference Required Required Deadline 30 November 2026 Year-round Examples of Previous Visiting Fellows The Centre has hosted Visiting Fellows from a wide range of academic and professional backgrounds and countries. Previous fellows have researched topics including: Statelessness and citizenship Statelessness among Rohingya communities Statelessness in the Middle East and North Africa Statelessness in Australia and New Zealand Climate displacement and nationality Statelessness and gender Statelessness among Roma communities Childhood statelessness Legal clinics addressing statelessness Denial of identity documents Statelessness and migration Statelessness and nationality laws Statelessness among displaced populations The list of previous fellows demonstrates the broad range of disciplines and geographic contexts that can be connected to statelessness research. A Globally Oriented Fellowship Previous Visiting Fellows have come from institutions and organisations in countries including: Australia Austria Belgium Germany India Italy Myanmar New Zealand Pakistan Poland Singapore Thailand The Netherlands United Kingdom United States The Centre s previous fellowship cohort also demonstrates that statelessness can be studied from multiple disciplinary perspectives, including law, political science, sociology, anthropology, history, philosophy and professional practice. Why This Fellowship Is Valuable The Peter McMullin Centre Visiting Fellowship can provide researchers and professionals with an opportunity to spend dedicated time developing a statelessness-related research project while engaging with an international research community. The combination of funding, research facilities and collaboration can be particularly valuable for applicants who want to: Advance an existing research project Develop a new research collaboration Work with researchers specialising in statelessness Receive feedback on research Present their work to an academic or public audience Build international professional connections Explore applied research approaches Contribute to global discussions on statelessness The opportunity also provides a platform for researchers to bring perspectives from their own countries, communities and professional environments into international statelessness research. Click HERE to read more and Apply. Conclusion The 2027 Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness Visiting Fellowship is a funded research opportunity for academics, researchers, practitioners and educators working on statelessness or closely related issues. The selected funded Visiting Fellow can receive up to AUD 6,000 toward international travel and accommodation in Melbourne and undertake a suggested one- to two-month research visit between August and October 2027 . During the fellowship, the Visiting Fellow will have access to workspace, library and computer facilities and will be expected to participate actively in the Centre s activities, present their research and contribute to the Centre s broader intellectual community. The opportunity is open across career stages, from postdoctoral early-career researchers to established and tenured academics , while relevant non-academic professionals are also encouraged to apply. Researchers with lived experience of statelessness are particularly encouraged to submit applications. For those interested in conducting research related to statelessness while developing international collaborations, the fellowship offers a valuable opportunity to engage with a specialist research centre in Melbourne. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Click HERE for more fellowship opportunities. title: CFR Fellowships 2027–2028: Paid Council on Foreign Relations Opportunities for Foreign Policy Professionals, Journalists, Technologists and Researchers
summary: Professionals seeking to build influential careers in foreign policy, international affairs, national security, journalism, technology, diplomacy and policy research should have the Council on Foreign Relations Fellowships on their radar for the 2027–2028 cycle. The Council on Foreign Relations, commonly known as CFR, operates an extensive portfolio of fellowship programs intended to give accomplished professionals opportunities to move beyond their usual professional environments, deepen their policy expertise, build international networks and gain direct exposure to policymaking, research or overseas institutions. CFR describes its fellowships as transformational opportunities for professionals with a demonstrated commitment to careers in foreign policy. Depending on the program, selected fellows may work at CFR itself, within policymaking institutions, at international organizations or at host organizations overseas. The opportunities are particularly notable because several provide substantial financial support. Depending on the fellowship, awards can include annual stipends of approximately $90,000 to $120,000 , monthly stipends, travel assistance, or—in the case of the Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship—a ten-month salary of $143,325 plus potential relocation assistance and employment benefits. However, applicants need to pay close attention to the individual program requirements. CFR does not operate one universal fellowship application. Each fellowship has its own target audience, professional requirements, research focus, placement arrangement and selection criteria. Current Application Status for CFR Fellowships 2027–2028 Prospective applicants should carefully distinguish between the current fellowship year and the next application cycle. As of August 2026, CFR states that the application window for many 2026–2027 fellowship programs is already closed . Eligible candidates are instead being advised to apply when applications open in fall 2026 for the 2027–2028 fellowship cycle . CFR has not yet listed a single universal closing date for the upcoming cycle on the fellowship pages reviewed. Candidates should therefore monitor the official CFR fellowship pages and, where available, subscribe to fellowship application alerts. The International Affairs Fellowship in India is an important exception: CFR currently states that the program is not accepting applications for the 2027–2028 fellowship year . Types of Fellowships Available Through CFR CFR divides its fellowship opportunities into several broad groups. Overseas Fellowship Programs These programs allow selected professionals to spend significant periods working and conducting research abroad. Current programs listed by CFR include: International Affairs Fellowship in Canada International Affairs Fellowship in India International Affairs Fellowship in Indonesia International Affairs Fellowship in Japan Chung Mong-Koo International Affairs Fellowship in the Republic of Korea Robert A. Belfer International Affairs Fellowship in European Security Domestic Fellowship Programs CFR also offers fellowship opportunities primarily based in the United States, including: International Affairs Fellowship Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship Fellowships Available Through Nomination or Invitation Several specialized CFR fellowships do not use the same public competitive application process. These include: Historian-in-Residence Fellowship Military Fellowship National Intelligence Fellowship State Department Fellowship on Technology Diplomacy Together, these programs allow CFR to engage professionals from government, academia, journalism, technology, research, security and other fields relevant to international affairs. 1. International Affairs Fellowship The flagship International Affairs Fellowship , or IAF, dates back to 1967 and is designed to bridge the divide between studying foreign policy and actually participating in policymaking. The fellowship aims to develop scholar-practitioners by allowing successful applicants to work in an environment substantially different from their regular professional setting. CFR reports that the program has produced more than 550 alumni, including senior government officials, diplomats, scholars and leaders from multiple sectors. Fellowship Structure The program operates through two major tracks. Government Track Professionals coming from academia or the private sector may spend the fellowship working in the U.S. government or at an international organization located in New York or Washington, DC. Applicants identify potential placement preferences and are encouraged to explore host organizations early. Some U.S. government placements may require security clearance. CFR Track Applicants coming from the federal government or U.S. military can be placed within CFR itself. These fellows conduct research, produce written work and contribute to policy-related projects alongside CFR experts and staff. The fellowship is designed as a full-time and largely in-person experience. Financial Support The fellowship: Lasts approximately 12 months Normally begins in September Provides a $120,000 stipend Includes a modest travel grant Fellows are treated as independent contractors rather than CFR employees and therefore do not receive normal employment benefits such as health insurance through the fellowship. Basic Eligibility Applicants must generally: Be U.S. citizens Be mid-career professionals Demonstrate a strong record of professional achievement Have substantial grounding in foreign policy Hold at least a bachelor s degree or equivalent Not apply for another CFR fellowship during the same application year CFR does not require a PhD for university applicants, although successful academic candidates often possess advanced qualifications. Application Requirements Applicants are generally expected to provide: Biographical information Education and employment history Two letters of support Proposed placements and a proposed work focus, where applicable Or a policy-relevant research proposal for applicants from the federal government and U.S. military CFR typically awards approximately eight to ten International Affairs Fellowships each year , making this one of the larger fellowship cohorts within its portfolio. 2. International Affairs Fellowship in Canada The International Affairs Fellowship in Canada was launched in 2016 and is sponsored by Power Corporation of Canada. The fellowship aims to deepen mutual understanding between emerging leaders in the United States and Canada. Selected mid-career U.S. professionals spend between six and twelve months at a Canadian institution while developing deeper expertise in Canada and U.S.-Canada relations. Professionals from fields including academia, government, business, journalism, NGOs and think tanks are encouraged to apply. Previous experience working on Canadian issues is not required. Financial Support The program provides: A fellowship period of six to twelve months A $110,000 stipend for 12 months A prorated stipend for shorter placements A modest travel allowance The fellowship is designed as a full-time, in-person experience, and fellows should normally expect substantial on-site participation with their Canadian host institution. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be U.S. citizens Be mid-career professionals Have a strong record of professional achievement Demonstrate commitment to a foreign-policy career Show interest in U.S.-Canada relations Hold at least a bachelor s degree Possess an appropriate U.S. passport valid beyond the fellowship period CFR normally awards approximately one to two fellowships each year . 3. International Affairs Fellowship in India The International Affairs Fellowship in India was created with support from Bharti Enterprises and aims to strengthen relations and professional understanding between rising leaders in India and the United States. Selected U.S. professionals can spend between three and twelve months conducting research in India, establishing professional networks and developing deeper knowledge of Indian politics, society and international affairs. Candidates can come from academia, business, government, journalism, NGOs and think tanks. Prior India experience is not mandatory, and knowledge of Hindi or another local language is not required. Fellowship Funding The fellowship provides: Three to twelve months in India Up to $90,000 for a 12-month fellowship A prorated amount for shorter periods A modest travel allowance CFR may assist fellows in identifying suitable host organizations in India. Important 2027–2028 Status Applicants should take particular notice of the current status of this program. CFR presently states that the International Affairs Fellowship in India is not accepting applications for the 2027–2028 fellowship year. Candidates interested specifically in India should therefore monitor CFR for future announcements rather than assuming applications will open with the other IAF programs. 4. International Affairs Fellowship in Indonesia The International Affairs Fellowship in Indonesia enables mid-career U.S. professionals to spend between three and twelve months conducting research and developing professional relationships in Indonesia. The program is sponsored by Yayasan Persahabatan Indonesia Amerika Serikat, or the Indonesia-USA Friendship Foundation. Professionals from academia, business, government, journalism, NGOs and think tanks can be considered. Prior experience working on Indonesia is not required. Financial Benefits Successful fellows may receive: Up to $110,000 for a 12-month fellowship A prorated stipend for shorter fellowship periods A modest travel grant The program is designed as a full-time, in-person experience. Eligibility Candidates generally need to: Be U.S. citizens Be mid-career professionals Hold at least a bachelor s degree Demonstrate strong professional achievement Show commitment to a foreign-policy career Demonstrate interest in U.S.-Indonesia relations Hold a valid U.S. passport meeting fellowship requirements Knowledge of Bahasa Indonesia is not required. CFR generally awards one to two fellowships annually under this program. 5. International Affairs Fellowship in Japan Founded in 1997 and sponsored by Hitachi, Ltd., the International Affairs Fellowship in Japan focuses on strengthening cooperation between rising leaders in the United States and Japan. The fellowship allows mid-career professionals to conduct research at Japanese host institutions on geopolitical and policy issues affecting U.S.-Japan relations. Possible areas of focus can include matters such as: National security Defense International trade Critical minerals Emerging technologies Export controls Other strategic issues affecting U.S.-Japan relations Applicants may come from academia, business, government, media, NGOs and think tanks. Fellowship Benefits The program provides: Three to twelve months in Japan A monthly stipend of $7,700 A $5,000 travel grant The program is full-time and intended to be conducted primarily in person at the fellow s Japanese host institution. Eligibility Applicants must generally: Be U.S. citizens Be mid-career professionals Have a strong professional record Have an interest in U.S.-Japan relations Hold at least a bachelor s degree Possess an appropriately valid U.S. passport Knowledge of Japanese is not required . CFR generally awards approximately three to five fellowships per year , making the Japan program one of the larger overseas IAF programs. 6. Chung Mong-Koo International Affairs Fellowship in the Republic of Korea The Chung Mong-Koo International Affairs Fellowship in the Republic of Korea , sponsored by Hyundai Motor Company, focuses on strengthening ties between emerging leaders in the United States and South Korea. Selected mid-career professionals can spend between three and twelve months conducting research in South Korea, developing professional networks and contributing to public discussion surrounding U.S.-Republic of Korea relations. Financial Support The fellowship offers: Three to twelve months in South Korea A monthly stipend of $10,000 The program is intended to be full-time and in person. Eligibility Applicants should generally: Be U.S. citizens Be mid-career professionals Demonstrate strong professional achievement Have an interest in U.S.-ROK relations Hold at least a bachelor s degree Hold an appropriately valid U.S. passport Knowledge of Korean is not required. Application Period CFR states that eligible candidates can apply in fall 2026 for the 2027–2028 fellowship cycle , with awardees expected to be notified by spring 2027. A specific closing date is not currently stated on the fellowship page. Approximately one to two fellows are selected each year . 7. Robert A. Belfer International Affairs Fellowship in European Security The Robert A. Belfer International Affairs Fellowship in European Security enables mid-career U.S. professionals to spend several months working and conducting research in Europe. Potential host institutions may include: Think tanks Universities Government agencies International organizations The primary focus must relate to European security and the wider U.S.-European relationship. Fellowship Funding The fellowship runs for approximately four to twelve months and provides: Up to $120,000 for 12 months A prorated stipend for shorter programs A modest travel grant Applicant Profile Eligible applicants should generally: Be U.S. citizens Be mid-career professionals Have a strong professional record Demonstrate commitment to foreign policy Have an interest in European security Hold at least a bachelor s degree Possess an appropriately valid U.S. passport CFR gives preference to candidates who have not previously accumulated substantial professional experience in Europe. Approximately one to two fellowships are awarded annually . 8. Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship Journalists interested in international affairs have a specialized CFR opportunity through the Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship . Launched in 1949, the program is named after influential journalist Edward R. Murrow and is designed to support responsible, analytical international journalism. One fellowship is normally awarded each year to a distinguished foreign correspondent or editor. What the Fellow Does The selected journalist receives time and institutional support to pursue substantial independent work rather than remaining tied to routine daily reporting deadlines. Possible work can involve: Long-form writing In-depth research Foreign-policy analysis Another substantial body of journalistic or research work The fellow also participates in CFR s research and events community. Financial Benefits The fellowship: Begins in September Lasts approximately ten months Provides a $100,000 stipend Includes a modest travel grant The fellow may be based in New York or Washington, DC. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be U.S. citizens Have distinguished journalism credentials Have covered international news for print, broadcast or online media widely available in the United States Preference is given to senior-level professionals . Applicants generally submit a proposal describing the major foreign-policy or international issue they intend to examine, together with professional information and two letters of support. 9. Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship Researchers specializing in nuclear weapons and nuclear-security policy should consider the Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship . Sponsored by the Stanton Foundation, the program supports postdoctoral scholars conducting policy-relevant work concerning nuclear security. Relevant areas can include: Nuclear weapons Nuclear war Nuclear proliferation Nuclear terrorism Deterrence Nuclear force posture Nuclear coercion Nuclear energy where directly relevant to security Emerging technologies affecting nuclear systems The fellow spends approximately twelve months at CFR s New York or Washington, DC office. Fellowship Benefits For the 2027–2028 cycle , CFR states that the fellowship will provide a $110,000 stipend , paid in twelve monthly installments. The fellow also receives mentorship from a senior CFR researcher and is expected to produce at least one policy-relevant document during the fellowship year. Eligibility Applicants must generally: Be U.S. citizens Have received a PhD by the fellowship start date or be postdoctoral scholars Have previous research experience Demonstrate a serious interest in nuclear security CFR normally selects one Stanton Nuclear Security Fellow each year . 10. Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship One of CFR s particularly distinctive opportunities is the Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship . Sponsored by the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Fund for Strategic Innovation, the fellowship targets mid-career technology practitioners with deep technical expertise. Potential backgrounds can include: Artificial intelligence Software development Cybersecurity Data infrastructure Quantum computing Technology diplomacy Other advanced technology fields relevant to national security and foreign policy The program is intended to bridge the divide between technical practice and policymaking. Financial Package Unlike many CFR fellows who operate as independent contractors, the Technologist-in-Residence becomes a CFR employee. The program provides: A ten-month fellowship A $143,325 salary over ten months Relocation assistance where applicable CFR employment benefits subject to applicable rules A part-time research associate for research and administrative support The fellowship normally begins in September and is based in either New York or Washington, DC. Eligibility A significant distinction is that the program does not state U.S. citizenship as its primary eligibility requirement. Instead: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States Applicants should be mid-career professionals Preference may be given to candidates with science or engineering qualifications, or at least a bachelor s degree combined with strong expertise in a relevant technology field Candidates must demonstrate genuine technical experience CFR specifically emphasizes that relevant experience should extend beyond simply writing about technology or managing projects containing technology components. Strong candidates may have hands-on experience designing, building or deploying technical systems. 11. Historian-in-Residence Fellowship The Historian-in-Residence Fellowship is intended for distinguished historians interested in connecting historical scholarship with contemporary foreign-policy challenges. The fellowship is supported by a grant from David M. Rubenstein. Participants can work from CFR s New York or Washington, DC office and are expected to develop substantial historical scholarship, including work toward a book that extracts contemporary policy lessons from important historical events. Fellowship Responsibilities The historian may be expected to: Work on a significant book project Write articles and opinion pieces Lead meetings examining foreign-policy questions through historical analysis Participate in CFR s intellectual and policy activities The fellowship may run for up to 24 months . Salary is commensurate with experience and includes standard benefits. Eligibility and Application The program can include: University professors College professors Independent historians unaffiliated with a university Candidates need an outstanding or demonstrated record of historical writing and research. However, there is no ordinary public application process. Participation is by invitation only. 12. CFR Military Fellowship The CFR Military Fellowship provides selected officers from the United States armed services with an opportunity to spend a year in residence at CFR in New York. Participating services can include the: U.S. Army U.S. Air Force U.S. Space Force U.S. Navy U.S. Marine Corps U.S. Coast Guard The program provides officers an opportunity to deepen their understanding of international relations through research, study, CFR meetings and engagement with CFR s professional network. CFR normally awards approximately six Military Fellowships each year . This is not a conventional open fellowship application. Military leadership nominates outstanding officers from the respective services. Interested personnel should use their relevant military professional-development or posting channels to determine eligibility and nomination procedures. 13. National Intelligence Fellowship Established in 1999, the National Intelligence Fellowship provides a senior U.S. intelligence officer an opportunity to engage with CFR s work on international affairs. The selected fellow interacts with CFR researchers, members and experts while developing a broader understanding of the political, military, diplomatic and economic dimensions of international affairs. At the same time, the fellow contributes intelligence-community expertise to CFR s understanding of national security and foreign policy. This is also a nomination-based opportunity. Candidates from the intelligence community are nominated through the Office of the Director of National Intelligence before being interviewed by CFR. Interested candidates should therefore pursue the appropriate internal government process rather than attempting to submit a standard public CFR fellowship application. 14. State Department Fellowship on Technology Diplomacy Established in 2024, the State Department Fellowship on Technology Diplomacy addresses the growing relationship between technological change, diplomacy and national security. The program enables an eligible U.S. Department of State professional to spend a year at CFR s New York or Washington, DC offices. Research can address key technology-policy priorities involving areas such as: Cyber policy Digital policy Emerging technologies Technology and national security Technology diplomacy The fellow participates extensively in CFR s meetings, research community and policy discussions. Who Can Participate? This program has highly specific eligibility. It is open only to U.S. Department of State direct-hire employees . Interested candidates are directed to the appropriate professional-development unit within the State Department for detailed eligibility and application procedures. How Much Funding Do CFR Fellowships Provide? Financial packages vary considerably across programs. Some of the publicly stated awards include: International Affairs Fellowship: $120,000 IAF in Canada: $110,000 for 12 months IAF in India: $90,000 for 12 months , although the program is not accepting 2027–2028 applications IAF in Indonesia: $110,000 for 12 months IAF in Japan: $7,700 per month plus a $5,000 travel grant IAF in the Republic of Korea: $10,000 per month Robert A. Belfer IAF in European Security: $120,000 for 12 months Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship: $100,000 Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship: $110,000 for 2027–2028 Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship: $143,325 salary over ten months Historian-in-Residence Fellowship: salary commensurate with experience Amounts for shorter overseas fellowship periods are generally prorated where CFR specifically provides for shorter placements. Who Should Consider Applying? The CFR fellowship portfolio is particularly relevant to established or emerging leaders whose professional work intersects with international affairs. Depending on the particular fellowship, suitable professional backgrounds may include: Government Foreign policy Diplomacy Academia International relations National security Business Think tanks Nonprofit organizations Journalism International reporting Artificial intelligence Cybersecurity Software engineering Data infrastructure Nuclear-security research Military service Intelligence History Technology policy Many of the open competitive fellowships focus on mid-career professionals , which means they should not automatically be treated as entry-level opportunities for recent graduates. Applicants need to review the requirements of their chosen fellowship carefully before preparing an application. Common Application Requirements Although exact requirements differ, many publicly competitive CFR fellowships require some combination of the following: Basic personal and biographical information Academic history Employment and professional history A research or project proposal Proposed host institution or placement information Explanation of the applicant s foreign-policy interests Explanation of how the fellowship will contribute to professional development Two letters of support Overseas fellowships commonly require project proposals connected with the relevant bilateral relationship or region. Specialist programs require more focused proposals. For example, Stanton applicants propose nuclear-security research, while Technologist-in-Residence applicants focus on the relationship between technology, foreign policy and national security. How CFR Selects Fellows CFR describes its competitive fellowship selection processes as highly selective. Although individual criteria vary, successful applications are generally assessed according to considerations such as: Professional accomplishments Scholarly qualifications where relevant Demonstrated engagement with foreign policy Quality and originality of the proposal Feasibility of the proposed work Relevance to the fellowship s geographic or thematic focus Potential contribution to the applicant s career development Ability to benefit from a different professional environment Potential for cross-cultural engagement, particularly for overseas programs For several programs, CFR also states that preference is given to applicants who have not previously received a CFR fellowship . Important Difference Between a Fellowship and a Degree Program Applicants should understand that most CFR fellowships are professional-development opportunities rather than academic scholarships. Several programs explicitly state that they do not finance: Pre-doctoral research Postdoctoral research where the fellowship is not specifically designed for postdoctoral scholars Work toward obtaining an academic degree Completion of projects on which substantial work has already been undertaken The objective is typically to create a transformational professional experience that takes the fellow into a new professional environment and develops new expertise, research or policy experience. The Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship is a notable specialist exception because it is specifically structured for PhD-level and postdoctoral nuclear-security scholars. Deadline and Application Timeline for CFR Fellowships 2027–2028 Prospective candidates should pay close attention to the cycle they are viewing. For many CFR programs: 2026–2027 applications: Closed. 2027–2028 applications: Expected to become available in fall 2026 . Selection notification: CFR states for several programs that successful applicants will be notified by spring 2027 . At present, the official pages reviewed do not publish one common final application deadline for the 2027–2028 cycle. Candidates should therefore monitor CFR s individual fellowship pages rather than relying on an old deadline from a previous application cycle. Candidates may also register for CFR s application alerts where these are available. Again, applicants interested in India should note that CFR specifically says the International Affairs Fellowship in India will not accept applications for 2027–2028 . How to Prepare Before Applications Open Candidates interested in the upcoming cycle can use the period before applications open strategically. Click HERE , for more information. 1. Identify the Correct Fellowship Do not apply simply because a fellowship offers a large stipend. Your professional history and proposed work must closely match the fellowship s objectives. A cybersecurity engineer, international journalist, nuclear-policy researcher and U.S.-Canada specialist should not necessarily target the same program. 2. Develop a Focused Proposal For proposal-based programs, applicants should identify a policy issue that is: Significant Timely Feasible Connected to the fellowship s objectives Relevant to the applicant s professional trajectory 3. Demonstrate Career Impact Applicants should be able to explain why spending several months away from their current professional environment will materially expand their expertise. The application should establish what the candidate can learn, contribute and ultimately bring back into their professional career. 4. Prepare Strong Letters of Support Many CFR fellowship applications require two letters of support . Potential referees should understand both the applicant s accomplishments and why the proposed fellowship represents a meaningful progression in the candidate s professional trajectory. 5. Research Potential Placements Applicants for overseas or government-track opportunities may benefit from researching institutions where their project could realistically be undertaken. A strong proposal is more persuasive when the proposed placement clearly aligns with the research question and fellowship objectives. Why CFR Fellowships Are Valuable for Foreign-Policy Professionals CFR fellowships combine several elements rarely found within a single professional-development opportunity. Successful fellows may gain: Dedicated time for policy research Direct exposure to policymaking institutions International experience Access to experienced foreign-policy professionals Opportunities to publish policy-relevant work Professional networking Cross-sector experience Experience working in a substantially different institutional environment Significant financial support Potential long-term career development in foreign policy and national security The value therefore extends beyond the financial award. The fellowship experience is designed to influence how participants approach policy, scholarship, technology, journalism or public service after completing the program. Official Fellowship Information Candidates should use the official Council on Foreign Relations Fellowships page as the primary source for current programs, application availability, eligibility requirements and future deadline announcements. Because individual fellowship conditions can change between application cycles, applicants should check their selected program again when the 2027–2028 application window formally opens. Conclusion The Council on Foreign Relations Fellowships 2027–2028 represent a diverse collection of high-level professional-development opportunities for people working across foreign policy, government, journalism, academia, national security, technology, nuclear-security research and related disciplines. CFR s portfolio includes overseas opportunities in Canada, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea and Europe, as well as domestic programs for foreign-policy professionals, journalists, nuclear-security scholars and experienced technologists. Financial packages can be substantial. Depending on the program, fellows may receive stipends of up to $120,000, monthly overseas allowances, travel support or, in the Technologist-in-Residence program, a ten-month salary of $143,325. Most applicants should remember that these are not general scholarships for students. CFR s main fellowship portfolio is heavily oriented toward accomplished professionals—often at the mid-career level—who already demonstrate a credible record of achievement and a serious connection to foreign policy or the particular discipline covered by the fellowship. For candidates who meet those requirements, preparing early is advisable. Many 2026–2027 application windows have already closed, while CFR indicates that applications for numerous 2027–2028 programs will become available in fall 2026 . Applicants should watch the official CFR fellowship pages for the opening of applications and publication of exact deadlines. For more global opportunities, click HERE .
