title: PERIL Youth Advisory Council 2026: Apply to Shape Research on Online Harms, Polarization, Misogyny and Extremism
summary: The PERIL Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is now accepting applications from young people aged 18 to 24 who want to contribute their perspectives to research on online culture and emerging challenges affecting young people. The Youth Advisory Council brings together 8–10 young people who meet virtually every two to three months to discuss issues such as online polarization, online harms, misogyny, extremism and other emerging trends in digital culture. This is a low-lift volunteer opportunity designed to give young people a meaningful voice in research without requiring a major time commitment outside scheduled meetings. Council members bring their lived experiences and perspectives, while PERIL brings its research and expertise. Together, they work toward research and solutions that better reflect the realities facing young people today. What Is the PERIL Youth Advisory Council? The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is an advisory group established by PERIL to ensure that research and proposed solutions are informed by the experiences and perspectives of young people. The council consists of approximately 8–10 young people between the ages of 18 and 24 . Members meet virtually every 2–3 months and contribute their perspectives on developments in online culture and issues affecting young people. The council may provide feedback on: Research questions Research findings Proposed solutions Emerging issues and trends Concerns affecting young people How research reflects Gen Z experiences The goal is to ensure that PERIL s work is not developed without considering the voices of the people most directly affected by the rapidly changing online environment. Why the Youth Advisory Council Matters Young people are among the most active participants in today s digital environment. Social media platforms, online communities and digital communication increasingly influence how people form relationships, consume information and understand social and political issues. At the same time, young people may encounter challenges including: Online harassment and abuse Polarization Misogynistic content Extremist content Harmful online communities Stereotyping and discrimination Rapidly emerging online trends Other forms of digital harm Research into these issues can benefit from the direct perspectives of young people who understand how online culture develops and changes. The YAC therefore provides an opportunity for young people to contribute directly to research and help ensure that research questions and proposed solutions are relevant to real-world experiences. What Will Youth Advisory Council Members Do? Membership is intentionally designed to be a low-lift volunteer role . Members are not expected to undertake extensive research work outside the meetings. Instead, participants primarily contribute through their perspectives, discussion and feedback. Their responsibilities include: 1. Attend Quarterly-Style Virtual Meetings Members participate in virtual meetings approximately every two to three months . Meeting schedules are developed collaboratively with members, taking their availability into consideration. This makes the opportunity suitable for young people who may be studying, working or managing other responsibilities. 2. Share Your Perspective Members are expected to bring their personal perspectives and experiences to discussions. This could involve talking about how young people interact with online culture, discussing emerging trends or highlighting concerns that researchers may need to consider. 3. Respond to Research Prompts During meetings, members may be asked to respond to questions or research prompts. Participants can provide their thoughts based on their experiences and understanding of issues affecting young people. 4. Provide Feedback on Research YAC members may review and provide feedback on: Research questions Project findings Proposed solutions Emerging research priorities Their feedback can help researchers better understand whether their work reflects the realities experienced by young people. 5. Identify Emerging Concerns Members can help surface issues that may be affecting young people but have not yet received sufficient attention. This is particularly important in online environments, where trends and communities can develop quickly. Key Areas of Discussion The Youth Advisory Council will explore trends in online culture, including several sensitive and rapidly evolving areas. Online Polarization Online platforms can contribute to increasingly divided conversations and communities. YAC members may help researchers understand how polarization appears in young people s online experiences and how young people perceive these changes. Online Harms The council may discuss different forms of harm occurring in digital spaces. Young people s perspectives can help identify emerging problems and provide insight into how these experiences affect individuals and communities. Misogyny Misogynistic content and communities can have significant effects on online culture. YAC members can contribute perspectives that help researchers understand how young people encounter and respond to misogynistic ideas and behaviours online. Extremism The council may also discuss online extremism and emerging extremist trends. Young people s perspectives can help researchers better understand how online environments evolve and how harmful ideas may spread or influence young audiences. Emerging Online Trends The scope of the YAC is not limited to the issues currently identified. The council can also help identify new and emerging concerns affecting young people as online culture continues to change. What Is the Time Commitment? One of the key features of this opportunity is its low time commitment . Members meet virtually approximately every 2–3 months . Participants are expected to: Attend the scheduled meetings Prepare to contribute their perspectives Respond to research prompts Provide feedback during discussions There is no expectation that members work on projects outside the meetings . This makes the council potentially suitable for young people who want to contribute to meaningful research while continuing with university, employment, volunteering or other commitments. One-Year Membership YAC members serve for an initial one-year term . Members have the option to renew their membership once . Participants may also leave the council at any time. If a member decides to step down, they simply need to inform the team. This structure provides flexibility while allowing members to contribute meaningfully over an extended period. Is the Youth Advisory Council Paid? No. The YAC is an unpaid volunteer opportunity . There is no salary or stipend mentioned in the opportunity information. However, members have the opportunity to contribute directly to research, provide feedback to researchers and help shape work addressing important issues affecting young people. The experience may also provide an opportunity to develop skills in: Research engagement Communication Critical thinking Giving constructive feedback Advisory participation Understanding online social issues Collaborative discussion Support for Sensitive Discussions Some of the topics discussed by the Youth Advisory Council may be sensitive. These include issues such as online harms, misogyny, extremism and other difficult experiences. Participation in any particular discussion is entirely voluntary . Members can choose not to participate in a conversation if they do not feel comfortable discussing a particular subject. According to the opportunity information, support resources are shared with all members upon joining . This approach recognises that participants may have different experiences and comfort levels when discussing sensitive topics. Who Should Apply? The opportunity is particularly suited to young people who: Are between 18 and 24 years old Have an interest in online culture Want to contribute to research Are interested in issues affecting young people Have perspectives on digital communities and online experiences Want to help researchers better understand Gen Z experiences Can participate in virtual meetings every 2–3 months Are comfortable sharing perspectives and providing constructive feedback Applicants do not need to be professional researchers. The purpose of the council is specifically to bring young people s perspectives and lived experiences into the research process. How to Apply Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly. Applicants should apply by email. Application Email Applications should be sent to: perilresearch@american.edu Email Subject Line Use the following subject format: YAC Application First Name Last Name For example: YAC Application Jane Smith What to Include in Your Application Applicants should provide the following information: 1. First and Last Name Provide your full name. 2. Age You should state your current age. Applicants must fall within the specified 18–24 age range . 3. Location Provide your city and state . The supplied opportunity information specifically requests city and state rather than country or continent. 4. Why Are You Interested in Joining the YAC? Applicants should explain why they want to become a member of the Youth Advisory Council. The response must be no more than 300 words . A strong response could explain your interest in: Online culture Youth issues Research Digital communities Online harms Social issues Giving young people a voice Contributing to research and solutions 5. What Do You Hope to Get Out of the Experience? Applicants should explain what they hope to gain from participating in the council. This response should also be no more than 300 words . You might discuss goals such as developing research-related experience, learning from researchers, meeting other young people, contributing to meaningful projects or developing your communication and advisory skills. 6. Resume or CV Applicants should also attach their resume/CV . Application Review Process Applications are reviewed on a quarterly basis . The process includes: Submission of the application by email Review of applications Shortlisting of candidates Invitation to a short interview for shortlisted applicants Selection of Youth Advisory Council members Because applications are accepted on a rolling basis, interested applicants do not need to wait for a single annual application period. Is There an Application Deadline? There is no fixed deadline stated . Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly . This means interested applicants should consider applying as soon as possible rather than waiting for a specific closing date. Why Join the PERIL Youth Advisory Council? The YAC offers young people an opportunity to move beyond simply being subjects of research and instead become contributors to the research process. Members can help researchers understand what matters to young people and how emerging online issues are experienced in everyday life. The opportunity can provide participants with the chance to: Have their perspectives heard Contribute to research questions Give feedback on research findings Influence proposed solutions Help identify emerging issues Learn about research and advisory work Connect with other young people Contribute to discussions about safer online environments Perhaps most importantly, members can help ensure that research about young people is informed by young people themselves . Conclusion The PERIL Youth Advisory Council provides an opportunity for young people aged 18–24 to contribute directly to research examining online culture, polarization, online harms, misogyny, extremism and other emerging issues. With only virtual meetings every two to three months and no expectation of work outside meetings, the YAC has been intentionally designed as a low-lift volunteer opportunity . Members serve for one year, with the possibility of one renewal, and can provide meaningful input into research questions, findings, proposed solutions and emerging concerns. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly , giving interested young people the opportunity to apply throughout the year. For young people who want their experiences and perspectives to play a role in shaping research and conversations about the digital world, the PERIL Youth Advisory Council offers a meaningful way to shape the conversation and advise the research . title: UfM Med Youth Lab 2026: Fully Sponsored Entrepreneurship Skills Programme in Italy
summary: The Union for the Mediterranean (UfM) has opened applications for the third edition of the UfM Med Youth Lab , an introductory entrepreneurship and employability skills programme for university students and recent graduates across the Euro-Mediterranean region. The programme is designed specifically for young people aged 18–29 who are curious about entrepreneurship but have little or no previous experience in the field. Up to 30 young participants will take part in online training between October and December 2026, followed by practical, in-person workshops in Palermo, Italy, from 14–16 December 2026 . Participation is free of charge , while selected participants from eligible countries will receive financial support covering travel, visa and accommodation costs for the in-person component. About the UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 The UfM Med Youth Lab is a skills-building initiative organised by the Union for the Mediterranean , with the support of the German Development Cooperation (GIZ) and in partnership with the University of Palermo . The 2026 edition focuses on introducing young people to foundational concepts in entrepreneurship and employability . Rather than requiring applicants to already have a business or extensive entrepreneurial experience, the programme specifically targets beginners who want to understand entrepreneurship and develop practical skills they can use in their academic, professional and community activities. Through expert-led sessions, non-formal education, teamwork and peer learning, participants will develop their entrepreneurial mindset and strengthen practical transferable skills. What Participants Will Learn During the programme, participants will develop foundational knowledge and skills in: Entrepreneurial thinking and mindset Innovation Basic financial literacy Communication Problem-solving Employability Teamwork and peer learning The programme is designed to build participants confidence and help them understand how entrepreneurial thinking can be applied to real-life challenges. Training of Trainers Approach A distinctive feature of the 2026 edition is its Training of Trainers approach . Participants will receive support to design a simple introductory awareness session about entrepreneurship. They will then be encouraged to share this knowledge with other young people at the national or local level in 2027 . Participants are not expected to become professional entrepreneurship trainers or experts. Instead, the programme aims to equip them with enough knowledge and confidence to act as peer facilitators , introducing basic entrepreneurship concepts within their communities. This approach allows the impact of the programme to extend beyond the 30 selected participants. Programme Components The UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 consists of three main components: 1. Online Training October–December 2026 Selected participants will participate in online learning sessions covering entrepreneurship, innovation, financial literacy, communication and problem-solving. 2. In-Person Workshops 14–16 December 2026 The in-person component will take place in Palermo, Italy . The workshops will provide participants with opportunities for practical learning, teamwork, peer exchange and interaction with other young people from across the Mediterranean. 3. Follow-Up Activities 2027 Following the main programme, participants will be encouraged to share their newly acquired knowledge through introductory entrepreneurship awareness sessions with peers in their communities. Who Can Apply? Applicants must meet the following requirements: Be 18–29 years old at the time of application. Be a national and resident of a UfM Member State . Be currently enrolled in a university programme or have graduated no more than one year before the application deadline . Hold a valid travel document, such as a passport. Have at least B2-level English or equivalent ability to actively participate in discussions and group activities. Have little or no significant previous knowledge, training or professional experience in entrepreneurship. Be fully available to participate in both the online training and the in-person workshops in Palermo. The programme is specifically designed for beginners . Applicants with significant previous entrepreneurship training, experience running or funding a start-up, or professional experience working with business-support organisations are not eligible for selection . Participants from the 2024 and 2025 editions may also apply, provided they meet all eligibility requirements for the 2026 edition. Eligible Countries Selected participants from the following countries are eligible for full sponsorship of travel, visa and accommodation expenses associated with the in-person programme: 🇦🇱 Albania 🇩🇿 Algeria 🇧🇦 Bosnia and Herzegovina 🇪🇬 Egypt 🇯🇴 Jordan 🇱🇧 Lebanon 🇱🇾 Libya 🇲🇷 Mauritania 🇲🇪 Montenegro 🇲🇦 Morocco 🇲🇰 North Macedonia 🇵🇸 Palestine 🇸🇾 Syria 🇹🇳 Tunisia 🇹🇷 Türkiye For selected participants from these countries, travel, visa fees and accommodation for the in-person component in Palermo will be covered. What Makes This Opportunity Valuable? The programme provides young people with an opportunity to gain practical entrepreneurship knowledge without requiring them to already have a business idea, start-up or extensive entrepreneurial background. Participants will also benefit from: Practical entrepreneurship and employability skills Exposure to innovation and entrepreneurial thinking Basic financial literacy Communication and problem-solving skills Peer learning with young people from across the Mediterranean International networking and regional cooperation Hands-on learning in Palermo Experience developing a peer-focused entrepreneurship awareness session The programme also provides an opportunity for participants to bring what they learn back to their own communities. Background of the Programme The UfM Med Youth Lab was first launched in Fes, Morocco, in November 2024 . Its second edition combined online training with in-person workshops in Tirana, Albania , in September and October 2025. The first two editions focused primarily on project-development skills , helping young people transform ideas into structured project proposals. Building on lessons from these previous editions, the 2026 programme introduces a new emphasis on entrepreneurship and employability skills , while maintaining the initiative s focus on practical learning, peer exchange and regional cooperation. The programme forms part of the UfM s broader work to strengthen youth participation, skills development and access to opportunities across the Euro-Mediterranean region . It contributes to the objectives of the UfM Youth Strategy 2030 and the UfM Youth Agenda: Call for Action , which highlight the importance of education, employment, social inclusion and meaningful youth participation. Application Process Before applying, candidates should: Check that they meet all eligibility requirements. Review the financial coverage available to participants. Carefully read the application guidelines. Prepare the required attachments. Submit the completed application before the deadline. Application Deadline 📅 30 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST How to Apply Interested applicants can submit their applications through the official UfM Med Youth Lab application platform: 🔗 Apply for the UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 For questions or difficulties with the application process, applicants can contact: medyouthlab@ufmsecretariat.org Conclusion The UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for university students and recent graduates to gain foundational entrepreneurship and employability skills in an international learning environment. With free participation , online training, practical workshops in Palermo , and full travel, visa and accommodation support available to selected participants from eligible countries, the programme provides a strong opportunity for young people who are at the beginning of their entrepreneurial journey. Young people who meet the eligibility requirements and have little or no previous entrepreneurship experience are encouraged to apply before the 30 August 2026 deadline.
